Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him. | | | A Humanoid Robot You Have to See to Believe At CES, Nvidia’s CEO dropped a bombshell: “This is the ChatGPT moment for robotics.” What followed stunned even seasoned analysts.A humanoid robot—powered by advanced AI—demonstrated real-world tasks with shocking precision. | The footage? Real. Eye-opening. Rapidly evolving. Behind this leap: a little-known $7 company helping build the systems powering this movement. And here is a recently released a special briefing on a company they believe deserves a closer look in this fast-moving sector. This isn’t sci-fi. It’s a milestone in the evolution of robotics. | Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. body:
USPS workers have been pulling out all the stops to manage and deliver a huge volume of packages this time of year. They also diligently work to deliver all our normal mail, including the mail-in ballots we fight so hard to protect.
As a part of the Save the Post Office coalition, our partners at the American Postal Workers Union will physically deliver our messages of thanks directly to postal workers across the country.
Please, before the calendar flips to 2026, send a personal message of thanks to these hardworking USPS employees >> [https://actionnetwork.org/forms/thank-postal-workers/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
SIGN HERE NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/forms/thank-postal-workers/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Folks,
Postal workers have continued to deliver for us through a particularly brutal year.
Their official motto is “neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night” will stop the Postal Service, but they also have delivered through aggressive political attacks, job cuts, service slowdowns, and nonstop pressure from Donald Trump, who calls the USPS a “tremendous loser” and tried to shove it under the Commerce Department and fire the board to pave the way for privatization.
Yet they deliver for all of us. Let’s deliver messages of gratitude directly to postal workers across the country, on their routes, in sorting centers, at distribution hubs, and in local post offices.
Sign the card and add your words of support to thank our postal workers across the country today >> [https://actionnetwork.org/forms/thank-postal-workers/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
SIGN HERE NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/forms/thank-postal-workers/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
During the holiday season, their busiest time of the year, USPS workers move over 15 billion pieces of mail and packages, including more than 400 million packages in a single week, to every single ZIP code in the country.
Today, we can boost their spirits, and show them that the country values their service. When you sign, you can also write a personal note to share with workers. Our coalition partners at the American Postal Workers Union will deliver our messages of thanks directly to postal workers across the country.
Add your name and a personal message of thanks by clicking here >> [https://actionnetwork.org/forms/thank-postal-workers/?source=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

_**by Dr. Eric Lullove**_
For the past few years, the American healthcare landscape has felt deceptively stable. Record-high enrollment in the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and a surge of "zero-premium" plans suggested we had turned a corner on affordability.
But as we look toward 2026, the safety net is fraying. A combination of expiring federal subsidies, the exit of major national insurers, and a fundamental shift in how employer-based insurance works is creating a "perfect storm" that will hit the self-employed and lower-income families hardest.
Here is the breakdown of the 2026 healthcare "cliff" and what it means for your wallet.
* * *
### **1\. The Death of the "Enhanced" Subsidy**
The single biggest driver of this crisis is the expiration of the **Enhanced Premium Tax Credits (PTCs)** on December 31, 2025. These credits, originally part of the pandemic-era relief and extended by the Inflation Reduction Act, did two things: they capped premiums at 8.5% of income and opened up subsidies to middle-income earners (those above 400% of the Federal Poverty Level) for the first time.
**The Fallout:**
* **The "Subsidy Cliff" Returns:** Since Congress chose to expire the additional premium insurance subsidies -- that 8.5% cap vanishes. A self-employed couple in their 60s earning $85,000 could see their premiums jump from roughly **$600 a month to over $1,800 a month** --essentially a second mortgage.
* **Lower-Income Impact:** For those near the poverty line, $0 premium plans will likely become a thing of the past. Average net premiums are projected to **more than double** , rising from about $888 to over $1,900 annually.
* **The Uninsured Surge:** The Urban Institute estimates that **4.8 million people** will become uninsured in 2026 simply because they can no longer afford the "rate shock."

* * *
### **2\. The Great Retreat: Aetna and UnitedHealthcare**
Affordability isn't just about subsidies; it's about competition. Unfortunately, the "big players" are heading for the exits.
**Aetna (CVS Health)** has officially confirmed it will stop offering individual and family ACA plans in **17 states** (including Florida, Texas, and Virginia) starting January 1, 2026. After a brief return to the market in 2022, the company cited a lack of profitability and the high cost of claims as reasons for the retreat.
**UnitedHealthcare and Humana** are following a similar "retrenchment" strategy, pulling back from hundreds of counties, particularly in their Medicare Advantage and certain ACA segments.
**Why this matters:** When national giants leave, they take their massive provider networks with them. Residents in affected areas will be forced into "narrower" networks offered by regional insurers, which often means losing access to specific specialists or hospitals.
* * *
### **3\. The "Under-Insurance" Trap in Employer Plans**
If you get your insurance through work, you might think you're safe. You're not. Employer health costs are projected to rise by **9% to 10% in 2026** --the third consecutive year of near-double-digit increases.
To keep their own costs down, employers are aggressively shifting the financial burden to employees through "plan design changes."
* **The Rise of High-Deductible Health Plans (HDHPs):** More companies are making HDHPs the _only_ option, meaning you may have to pay $3,000 to $6,000 out of pocket before your insurance kicks in a single cent.
* **Coinsurance vs. Copays:** We are seeing a shift away from $30 "flat" copays toward **20 -30% coinsurance**. On a $10,000 outpatient surgery, that's the difference between a small office fee and a $3,000 bill.
* **The "GLP-1" Surcharge:** The explosion in popularity of weight-loss drugs (like Ozempic and Wegovy) is a massive cost driver. Many employers are responding by tightening "prior authorization" rules or increasing the coinsurance specifically for these specialty drugs.

* * *
### **4\. The Self-Employed "Tax Trap"**
For freelancers and small business owners, 2026 brings a new technical danger: **Elimination of Repayment Limits.**
Previously, if a self-employed person underestimated their income, there was a "cap" on how much of the subsidy they had to pay back to the IRS. Starting in 2026, those caps are effectively gone. If your business has a surprisingly good year and pushes you over the 400% poverty threshold, you may be required to **repay every single dollar** of the subsidy you received--a "tax bill" that could easily reach $15,000 or more.
* * *
### **The Bottom Line**
2026 marks a pivot point where "having insurance" no longer equates to "having healthcare." Between the loss of subsidies and the rise of massive deductibles, millions of Americans are becoming **" under-insured"**--holding a card in their wallet they are too afraid to use because of the out-of-pocket costs.

And now I’m running for Secretary of State because 2028 is coming, and Colorado needs someone who already knows this job inside and out. This is a people-powered campaign. No corporate money. No shortcuts. Just Coloradans who believe our democracy belongs to all of us — not politicians who think they’re entitled to power. You’ve probably already heard that Trump has torn down a wing of the White House for his selfish aims. And what will go in its place? **A ballroom funded by private donors.** A project where the cost has ballooned from $200 million to $300 million, and now $400 million – all from individuals who are being kept secret from the public. That’s not just concerning, it’s unacceptable.
This is _dancing with the devil:_ private money, anonymous donors, and the potential for special access to power. Some donors were even reportedly invited to a private White House dinner only after pledging millions of dollars, with many of them holding significant business interests with the federal government.

This is not about petty politics. This is about ensuring we have an honest, just, and accountable administration for the greatest democracy on Earth. Wealthy insiders should never be able to waltz their way into the halls of the President’s House while we are left in the dark.

# [Ending the year, starting the fight](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=182629177&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTgyNjI5MTc3LCJpYXQiOjE3NjcxMDcxMTEsImV4cCI6MTc2OTY5OTExMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.gh07Uyh1S47Aqy-RmDgkO0fJYQV5BeG6sBS3Lfwe8Uo)
### This is what it's going to take in 2026
Dec 30
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL2VuZGluZy10aGUteWVhci1zdGFydGluZy10aGUtZmlnaHQ_.lUlWRHeJdja_7X6XXER4Mtb-vKpJDZ_KatqxTZ2jSxE?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/ending-the-year-starting-the-fight?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Hi friends,
It's hard to believe we're just a day away from closing out 2025. I don't know about you, but this year has felt both incredibly long and impossibly fast. Like it's been a decade, but also three weeks.
As I look back, one thing is certain: _**I 'm filled with gratitude.**_
Over the past year, I've met so many people across this great state. I'm thankful for every single conversation - for every person who shared their hopes, their worries, and their stories with me.
I carry those conversations with me every day. They're shaping the kind of grassroots campaign we're building and, if I have the honor, the kind of senator I'll be: rooted in service, focused on real solutions, and powered by people, not megadonors.
But I need to be honest with you: **2026 is going to be a battle.**
Michigan's open Senate seat will be one of the most competitive and expensive races in the country. It will likely determine who controls the U.S. Senate.
And with stakes this high, we know what's coming: MAGA megadonors are already lining up to spend tens of millions to flip this seat red and install Donald Trump's yes-man, Mike Rogers, in the Senate.
That's why this moment, and the next 24 hours, matters so much.
Tomorrow night is our **final FEC fundraising deadline of the year.** And it's our most important one yet. Because once the clock strikes midnight - this race kicks into high gear.
What we raise _right now_ will be shared publicly and determine how strong we are when the first attack ads hit the airwaves, when the debates begin, and when the national media really starts paying attention.
All our numbers will be analyzed. And the strength of this team, especially the people who've stood with me from the start, will set the tone for the fight ahead.
That's why I'm asking: **If you 're in a position to give - even just a few dollars - it would mean the world to me and our team. **Your support before this critical deadline will help us close the books strong, power our organizing operation, and show the GOP that Michigan's Senate seat isn't for sale.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c517ee6c-0f79-4964-a555-f99c56f6943f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But if now isn't the right time, that's OK too. Just being part of this campaign - showing up, staying engaged, sharing your voice - that _matters_.
We're building something special here. Not because it's easy, but because it's necessary. Because Michigan families deserve a senator who never stops fighting for them. Because our democracy is worth defending. **And because the future we believe in won 't build itself.**
Thank you. Thank you for standing with me, for believing in this campaign, and for helping us get closer to the future we're fighting for.
Get ready to make history in 2026.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c517ee6c-0f79-4964-a555-f99c56f6943f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

body:
We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the entire executive branch bearing down on me right now.
Hey Peter, it’s Mark Kelly.
Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run for the Senate.
I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy.
But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I had to do something.
So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support, we won that one, too.
I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help.
We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the entire executive branch bearing down on me right now.
After everything you’ve already done for me, I shouldn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Asking because I have to, not because I want to
body:
I wouldn’t be here without you.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/2365?source=&t=1&akid=232%2E124072%2Ex2Snz_)
Peter, There have been some hard days during my career working to serve North Carolina. Days when we couldn’t get done the things we set out to accomplish. Days that we couldn’t stop far-right legislation from hurting our people. But there have been many, many more days when we were able to make a difference together. Expanding Medicaid. Getting some raises for public school teachers. Paid parental leave. Bringing good-paying jobs to the state. _Those achievements matter._ There are hard days on the campaign trail, too. This is a competitive race, and the national GOP is aligned against us, trying to stop us from flipping this seat blue for the first time since 2008. Earlier this month, Donald Trump even called me out at one of his rallies. On the hardest days, knowing that you’re with me helps me keep up the fight. And no matter what, I am reminded that the opportunity to serve is itself the greatest privilege. Our nation deserves leaders who care about more than personal pride or party loyalty. Leaders who are ready to do real work, not just play petty grievance politics. The opportunity to fight for you as the next Senator from North Carolina would be an honor I could never repay — but I will spend every day trying. **[I wouldn’t ask for even more support from you unless it was urgent, and right now, it really is. Our fundraising deadline for our final public filing of 2025 is tomorrow, and we’re still short of our $1 million online fundraising goal. I know that sounds like a lot, but it’s what we need to raise to stay competitive against my far-right opponent and the mega-donors backing him. Please, donate anything you can spare before the deadline.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/3499?t=7&akid=232%2E124072%2Ex2Snz_)** | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/3499?t=8&akid=232%2E124072%2Ex2Snz_)

Roy Cooper

---
Friend — it’s Ilhan. As you probably know, our FEC fundraising deadline is tomorrow at midnight. **[I’m humbly asking for your support before tomorrow.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-dec25.HnwiDc&refcode=em251230-1-210&t=3&akid=2015%2E791427%2Elyi71B) Friend, this has never been easy. I was raised in a refugee camp, immigrated to the US, and found a good life in Minnesota. I got active in my community and eventually earned the privilege of serving and representing my neighbors in office. Since then I’ve faced attacks and harassment from some of the most powerful people in the world; the President, the Vice President, members of Congress, foreign leaders, oligarchs, multi-billion dollar media outlets and corporations, you name it. I’ve dealt with the endless death threats, the insults, the people who think I’m not good enough, or not ‘from here’, and want me to hide away from public life. **But through all of this, I’ve never backed down. Because I have YOU.** This entire team and the movement we’ve built together has helped me push through and keep up the fight for our futures. Because our progressive vision for this nation, where everyone is taken care of and provided the rights and dignity they deserve, is worth fighting for, despite it all. So, with this crucial FEC deadline tomorrow, I’m counting on you to stand by my side as you always have. **[I’m humbly asking you to make a contribution of $10 or whatever you can afford today. Team Kelly here—we hope you’re enjoying your holiday season! We wanted to reach out with some exciting news— Ms. Magazine named Kelly as a ‘Top Feminist’ for 2025 ! She is listed alongside an incredible group of leaders, and is deeply honored to be featured.

If you know anything about Abdul, you know he takes his coffee seriously.

It’s not necessarily the quickest way to start your morning, but the end

That’s how this campaign works, too.

AIPAC or corporate PACs. That means no pre-packaged talking points. No
watered-down positions. Just clear, focused priorities:

* Putting more money in your pocket

* Passing Medicare for All

Most campaigns today are mass-produced — funded by the same big-money
groups, designed to say as little as possible. That’s not us. We’re
counting on the people reading this email to fuel this campaign by filling
up our cup before the new year:

| | Friend, as 2025 comes to a close, I want to highlight what is most important as we head into the new year. **We'll be defending against Donald Trump and Republicans' attempts to cut healthcare, privatize Social Security and Medicare, and pursue policies that raise costs for American families.** It's going to be a difficult fight, and to win, we need to stand together.
---
| | [ STAND WITH ME ➜ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122262729/592069553/1060786640?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NDk5NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOTBiMTRhZS05NmU1LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uQorRwY2URM5Wrvp2uGvHdQQ9XXmtwo8z7hKSYvf50o=)
---
My priority as a Member of Congress will always be to stand up for those who need an ally in Washington. For working families and neighborhoods in Philadelphia, my promise remains the same today as the day I took office: **I'm here to work for you, and it's a privilege to fight for Philadelphia and Pennsylvania in Washington.** **As we wrap up this year, I'm asking one last time for your support. We have a big task to restore a Democratic House majority in 2026, and that work begins right now.** So in addition to wishing you and your family a happy new year, I hope you'll stand with me as we enter 2026. It means so much to have you on our team as we continue to work for the American people. Sincerely, Congressman Brendan Boyle

name: Gavin Newsom
subject: The end of Trump's presidency
body:
We have to finish the job.

In just a moment, I am going to ask you to split a contribution between
Mike McGuire for Congress and Congressman Adam Gray before tomorrow's FEC
fundraising deadline comes to a close. Please let me explain why this
request is so important... especially today.

Here is the truth:

We passed Proposition 50 to stop Donald Trump from rigging the next
election before a single vote was cast.

The victory gives us a good chance to flip 5 Republican seats in the next
election. But doing so made a few Democratic seats more competitive than
they were.

So if we are going to actually realize the promise of what we accomplished
and take back the House -- effectively ending Trump's presidency -- then
we have to finish the job.

Mike McGuire is the candidate we need to defeat the Republican incumbent
in a new district and Adam Gray is a Democratic Congressman we need to
help hold his seat in his new district. Both need our help.

If they can file huge FEC reports after tomorrow's deadline, there's a
good chance we can scare off Republican spending in this race. So while I
don't plan on sending a million fundraising emails going forward, this one
was important enough to ask. We can take two seats off the board today.

contribution between Democrat Mike McGuire and Adam Gray's campaigns for
Congress in California. Your donation can effectively end Trump's
presidency if we take back the House.

If you've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution

* Rioting in cities across America and burning Old Glory

[] [] [] December 30, 2025 • Newsletter [] Mike Rowe on What America Needs Most Moms for America Weekly Podcast [] [] Moms for America Weekly Podcast [-] You probably know Mike Rowe as the host of "Dirty Jobs." The show was a surprise hit, and following its success, Mike has become one of the leading champions of training in the skilled trades. These are the essential jobs that make our nation run. We're revisiting this episode of the Moms for America Podcast in which Mike shares his vision for education and the unlikely path that led him to his successful career. Like, subscribe and share. View the Podcast [] Listen to the Podcast [] Listen to the Podcast on Spotify [] Moms for America Weekly Blog [] [] Debunking 5 Popular Lies Could Be Key to Your Family’s Future In 2026, it is the patriotic Americans like you who are countercultural. We are willing to stand for the Truth against any and all lies. We will admit our mistakes and own our shortcomings – but we will not shrink from the truth that history is on our side. As we prepare to celebrate our 250 years as a nation, our “Super-Centennial” as some are calling it, we're taking a look at five lies in our culture that we must reject in order to be strong and successful. Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Our voter registration work doesn't ever end, folks.
Despite vote-suppressing state legislatures making it harder to register to vote -- passing bills to stop organizations like ours and our partners on the ground from helping potential voters navigate the increasingly murky rules around voter registration -- we're still pulling out all the stops to bring voters into the system.
Voter registration is a critical part of grassroots efforts to protect voting rights. The more people who vote, the more our government looks like we, the people. But to get to the point where every voice is heard, we need your help .
Just $3 can help us register a new voter. Will you step up with $24 or more today to help register 8 new voters? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=123025_1&amount=24]

Voter participation has been increasing, and young people -- a major target of opponents of voting rights -- see the importance of voting now more than ever. Voting quickly becomes a habit -- a habit our democracy sorely needs to fulfill the promise of the American dream. Overwhelming key states with new voter registrations can help turn the tide against the voter suppression laws we've seen passed the last few years.
The next election will determine whether our democracy stays mired in the darkness and conspiracy theories we hear every day or if we can reclaim our rights -- from voting to choice and more -- and march forward to a better future.
New voter registration -- at just about $3 per new voter -- can be game-changing. Can you pitch in with $24 or whatever you can to help us register a wave of new voters ahead of voter registration deadlines? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=123025_1&amount=24]

# **Minnesota "Learing Center" 2015 surveillance footage shows parents signing kids in then leaving immediately**
Shocking unearthed surveillance footage from 2015, which came to light in a 2018 state fraud case, shows Minnesota parents dropping their children off at day care centers, signing them in so providers could bill the state for full days of care, and **[then leaving with the kids moments later](https://substack.com/redirect/787ef458-9cfd-4b8f-b4c3-b83151933922?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , with some days seeing no families show up at all while day cares still claimed government reimbursements, and alleged phony centers giving kickbacks to participating parents.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/787ef458-9cfd-4b8f-b4c3-b83151933922?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Artistic recreation, not surveillance footage
* **Video resurfaces amid viral expos e of inactive centers:** The 2015 clips resurfaced amid outrage sparked by independent journalist Nick Shirley's viral video showing multiple Minnesota child care centers that received millions in state funding despite appearing inactive, including one with a misspelled "Quality Learing Center" sign, as US Education Secretary Linda McMahon called the alleged fraud a "breathtaking failure."
* **FBI deploys resources as fraud schemes tied to Somali community:** FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency has deployed personnel and investigative resources to Minnesota to "dismantle large-scale fraud schemes exploiting federal programs," calling child care allegations "just the tip of a very large iceberg" and threatening convicted Somali scammers with deportation, as the scams have been largely tied to Minnesota's migrant Somali community and Gov. Tim Walz faces fire over other alleged Medicaid-funded disability schemes.

# **$5.8 billion in "questionable payments" from Biden era HUD to deceased and non-citizens**
A HUD report for fiscal year 2025 revealed that out of $50 billion in federal rental assistance distributed in FY 2024, $5.8 billion **[went to"questionable" recipients](https://substack.com/redirect/2b55f8d8-0d00-48c3-901c-087037ae2c81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** including approximately 30,000 deceased tenants who were either actively enrolled or received assistance after death, and thousands of potential non-citizens, with a "large concentration" of funds going to New York, California, and Washington, D.C.
* **HUD Secretary blames Biden administration 's lack of oversight:** HUD Secretary Scott Turner stated the "massive abuse of taxpayer dollars not only occurred under President Biden's watch, but was effectively incentivized by his administration's failure to implement strong financial controls," with HUD's report alleging Biden directed the department "to push funding out the door with minimal oversight" and failed to provide tools to verify whether entities enforced rental assistance rules.
* **HUD investigating with potential criminal referrals:** HUD must now confirm whether fraud occurred and its extent before determining if funding should be paused or revoked and if criminal referrals are necessary, with an official telling the Post that "HUD is implementing processes and procedures to revoke or pause funding" and "could make criminal referrals and exercise other enforcement actions once it has confirmed fraud occurred."

* * *
# **Minnesota officials deny fraud after viral daycare video**
Minnesota Department of Children, Youth and Families Commissioner Tikki Brown said prior inspections of childcare centers featured in Nick Shirley's viral video **["did not uncover fraud,"](https://substack.com/redirect/037f653b-a209-43eb-93ff-e9f210ad2963?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** stating each facility has been visited at least once in the past six months with inspectors finding children present during unannounced visits, and currently there is "no pause on payments to the centers named in the video."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f98fa4b3-aad6-4aae-9043-5f6d272e485d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Quality "Learing' Center manager forcefully rejects allegations:** Ibrahim Ali, manager of Quality Learning Center which appeared inactive in Shirley's video despite receiving roughly $4 million in state funds for 99 children, said "There's no fraud going on whatsoever," explaining the center operates Monday through Thursday from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. serving after-school children and has remained open for more than eight years, claiming the video "misrepresented the facility by filming outside posted hours."
* **Manager argues scrutiny unfairly targets Somali community:** Ali argued the allegations have been "damaging to the business and the broader Somali community," asking "Are you trying to record that we're doing fraud or are you trying to put the Somali name and the fraud in the same sentence? That's what really hurt us the last couple of days," while inviting media and inspectors to return during operating hours to observe normal activity.
* **Viral video sparks widespread backlash against Gov. Walz:** Shirley's 42-minute video showing what appears to be a largely inactive facility with a misspelled "Quality Learing Center" sign has sparked criticism of Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz from high-profile figures including Vice President JD Vance, Rep. Mike Lawler, Donald Trump Jr., and Elon Musk, with Shirley saying on Fox News the alleged fraud was "so obvious" that a "kindergartner could figure out that there is fraud going on."

A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." clean_body: Cook Political Report has FOUR U.S. Senate races currently rated as TOSS UPS for 2026: Georgia. Maine. Michigan. North Carolina. Georgia’s U.S. Senate seat is currently held by Democrat Jon Ossoff — the most vulnerable Democrat in the 2026 midterm elections. The GOP will undoubtedly do everything they can to win this seat back for a Republican. They’ll spend millions upon millions of dollars. They’ll come up with all sorts of outlandish attacks. Anything to solidify their majority in the Senate next year. Maine’s U.S. Senate seat is currently held by Republican Susan Collins — the most vulnerable Republican in the 2026 midterm elections. Cook Political Report recently UPGRADED this race from Leans Republican to TOSS UP, signaling that Democrats have a major opportunity to flip this seat. Now, we need to make sure we carry the momentum we've seen for Democrats in Maine + across the country all the way to next November. The good news is that Democrats currently hold every statewide seat in Michigan. But defending this critical Democrat-held Senate seat won't be easy. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Why I'm supporting Katie Porter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Katie Porter for Governor 2026
body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=40631%2E3422442%2Enbqow_)
Peter, it's Elizabeth Warren here.
In a minute, I’m going to ask you to **[make a donation to support Katie Porter’s campaign for governor in California. But first, I want to talk about why I’m supporting Katie, and why your support matters.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20251230_1_ak.nSedpZ&refcode=em20251230-40631&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=40631%2E3422442%2Enbqow_)**
Katie shares the lived experience of millions of Californians she’s running to represent — people who work hard, who want to raise healthy kids in good homes without it costing an arm and a leg, and who understand what it’s like to anxiously review their receipts after visiting the grocery store.
**Katie has what it takes to lead her state through this affordability crisis.**
But a statewide election in California requires a lot of money, and Katie can’t bankroll her own race with her billions of dollars. And she’s not taking contributions from corporations and lobbyists.
**[She’s counting on grassroots supporters to power her campaign and win in California. So, can you make a donation of $5 or whatever makes sense for you to support Katie’s campaign?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20251230_1_ak.nSedpZ&refcode=em20251230-40631&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=40631%2E3422442%2Enbqow_)**
[Donate ›››](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20251230_1_ak.nSedpZ&refcode=em20251230-40631&t=23&akid=40631%2E3422442%2Enbqow_)
I still remember the day when I met Katie. My consumer law class was early in the morning, meaning a lot of students had their heads down, trying to avoid being called on.
But not Katie. She was determined and ready to go. When the first answer she gave wasn’t her strongest, she came to my office hours and said, “Please keep calling on me. I am going to learn to do this.”
Getting to know her, I saw her bone-deep commitment to making a difference in people’s lives.
When Katie decided to run for Congress in 2018, I was very happy to support her. I knew that we needed more people like her in Washington — who understood the real struggles that working families faced, who had the courage to stand up to big corporations and special interests, and who would fight to make our government work for everyone.
A Democrat hadn’t represented her district for decades, but she knew exactly how to personally connect with voters, build a strong movement, and win. She flipped that seat, and she’s been winning for working people ever since.
Simply put, Katie delivers. She’s smart and she isn’t afraid. She stands up to Wall Street and Big Pharma, she holds fossil fuel companies accountable, and she fights to protect Californians’ rights against Trump’s far-right administration. She is exactly who Californians need as their next governor.
**[So please, if you can, make a donation of $5 or whatever makes sense to Katie’s campaign. We’re going to keep fighting to make our government work for working people — and we need you in this fight.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20251230_1_ak.nSedpZ&refcode=em20251230-40631&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=24&akid=40631%2E3422442%2Enbqow_)**
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

Katie is running to be California’s next governor because California and our country need a leader who will stand up to Trump to lower costs, protect our rights, and combat climate change. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4g-em-footer?refcode=em20251230-40631&amounts=&t=25&refcode2=40631_3422442_nbqow_&akid=40631%2E3422442%2Enbqow_)**

I knew that we needed more people like her in Washington — who understood the real struggles that working families faced, who had the courage to stand up to big corporations and special interests, and who would fight to make our government work for everyone. A Democrat hadn’t represented her district for decades, but she knew exactly how to personally connect with voters, build a strong movement, and win. She flipped that seat, and she’s been winning for working people ever since. Simply put, Katie delivers. She’s smart and she isn’t afraid. She stands up to Wall Street and Big Pharma, she holds fossil fuel companies accountable, and she fights to protect Californians’ rights against Trump’s far-right administration. She is exactly who Californians need as their next governor. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth Katie is running to be California’s next governor because California and our country need a leader who will stand up to Trump to lower costs, protect our rights, and combat climate change.

## Thank you for a great 2025...
As we head into 2026, I want to express some gratitude for all of the support this past year.
Whether you tuned in every show, subscribed to the newsletter (seanspicer.com), shared the links to the show or even just kept up with me on socials, I'm grateful for the time and support.
I couldn't do this without you.
So, as we get ready to start into the new year, I want to hear from you.
Thoughts on what we should focus on here in the newsletter, topics for shows, guest ideas, issues to cover-- I want to hear it all.
Some of my best shows have come from viewer suggestions, so I'm grateful for any ideas you want to share.
I've been in the game for over 30 years
I did my first congressional race in 1994, the year that Republicans won the House for the first time in 40 years.
I worked on Capitol Hill during the implementation of the Contract with America under the leadership of Newt Gingrich.
In 2002, I was the Director of Incumbent Retention at the National Republican Congressional Commitee when we defied history and kept the majority under a President who was in the White House.
I've seen it all and I want to share that insight with you. There a lot of great pundits out there -- many of whom I listen to regularly, but few if any have been in the game. I have. I have seen it from every angle - the campaign, the executive and the Capitol Hill.
As Trump gets ready for the second year of his second term, I'm betting there will be plenty to talk about.
So comment below what topics you'd like to see covered on the show, and here in the newsletter. I see all the emails you send at contact@seanspicer.com -- and I TRY to respond. If just a thought, a guest suggestion, I want you ideas and feedback.
Between your suggestions and the ideas my team is cooking up, this new year will be the best one yet.
Here's to a 2026 filled with--in the immortal words of President Trump--so many wins that we get tired of winning.

Then for the rest of the week we're throwing it back to some of our favorite shows of year, including conversations with Tim Parlatore, Victor Davis Hanson, Dr. Matt Oz, and more. Turn on notifications so you don't miss a show! Audio podcast help If you watch the show on YouTube, Rumble or X, please do me a HUGE favor -- can you click the link , hit subscribe and give us a 5-star review on Apple. It's super helpful. Thank you! Sponsor links... Head over to my new page, where you can find all the show discounts and codes! Thank you for a great 2025... As we head into 2026, I want to express some gratitude for all of the support this past year. Whether you tuned in every show, subscribed to the newsletter (seanspicer.com), shared the links to the show or even just kept up with me on socials, I'm grateful for the time and support. I couldn't do this without you. So, as we get ready to start into the new year, I want to hear from you. Thoughts on what we should focus on here in the newsletter, topics for shows, guest ideas, issues to cover-- I want to hear it all. Some of my best shows have come from viewer suggestions, so I'm grateful for any ideas you want to share. I've been in the game for over 30 years I did my first congressional race in 1994, the year that Republicans won the House for the first time in 40 years. I worked on Capitol Hill during the implementation of the Contract with America under the leadership of Newt Gingrich. In 2002, I was the Director of Incumbent Retention at the National Republican Congressional Commitee when we defied history and kept the majority under a President who was in the White House. I've seen it all and I want to share that insight with you. There a lot of great pundits out there -- many of whom I listen to regularly, but few if any have been in the game. I have. I have seen it from every angle - the campaign, the executive and the Capitol Hill. As Trump gets ready for the second year of his second term, I'm betting there will be plenty to talk about. So comment below what topics you'd like to see covered on the show, and here in the newsletter. I see all the emails you send at contact@seanspicer.com -- and I TRY to respond. If just a thought, a guest suggestion, I want you ideas and feedback. Between your suggestions and the ideas my team is cooking up, this new year will be the best one yet. Here's to a 2026 filled with--in the immortal words of President Trump--so many wins that we get tired of winning. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Peter,
Grassroots power doesn't build itself.
It’s built day-by-day, brick-by-brick, by organizers who are deeply committed to the well-being of their communities. It thrives through connections and coordination among members, supported by a strong network that can respond at a moment’s notice.
**That's what you funded this year:**

clean_body: You can help us build the organizing infrastructure our communities need in 2026. | | | | | This is one of your last chances to support our work this year. Your gift — whether it be $50 or $500 — directly funds the trainings, gatherings, and coordination that turn isolated organizers into a powerful, coordinated movement. | | Peter, Grassroots power doesn't build itself. It’s built day-by-day, brick-by-brick, by organizers who are deeply committed to the well-being of their communities. It thrives through connections and coordination among members, supported by a strong network that can respond at a moment’s notice. That's what you funded this year: Through Summer of Dreams and our Organizing Academy, we trained hundreds of young leaders in how to identify targets, build coalitions, and run effective campaigns. Our East Coast and West Coast membership gatherings brought undocumented young people together to share tactics and build the relationships that turn isolated local efforts into coordinated national power. At our National Power Building Retreat in Arizona, we used a train-the-trainer model to multiply our capacity — every person trained there became a trainer in their home community. The DMV Power Building Retreat strengthened organizing in one of our most critical regions, while Digital Congress connected thousands virtually to strategize across the country. This is how organizing power gets built: through the diligent process of training organizers, building relationships, and creating the infrastructure that allows us to act swiftly when needed. Cori here.
As we head into a new year, I’ve been thinking about resolutions. Not the symbolic ones, but the kind that actually change things.
Here’s one of mine:
In 2026, I’m proving that people power is stronger than AIPAC’s money – period. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251230_resolution_eoy3_act]
In fact, The New York Times reported what my team and I already knew: AIPAC’s grip on our politics is slipping. The tide is turning.
That doesn’t happen by accident. It happens because everyday people are organizing, giving what they can, and refusing to let special interests dictate our future.
And yet, my opponent is still clinging to the old playbook.
This year, 63% of my opponent’s campaign money came from AIPAC bundlers . It’s the clearest sign there is of who they answer to and whose interests they’re protecting.
Our movement is built by people, young people, Black and Brown communities, seniors, and everyday voters who believe our democracy should serve the many, not the highest bidder.
Tomorrow is my only end-of-year deadline of the cycle, and how we close it out will send a message that can’t be ignored. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251230_resolution_eoy3_act]
If we’re serious about starting the new year strong and showing AIPAC and their allies that our values are not for sale, this is the moment to act.
We are so close to meeting our goal before the deadline, and proving OUR movement can’t be silenced, but to do that, we are counting on you to make a $5, $10, or $25 donation before midnight TOMORROW. Are you with us? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251230_resolution_eoy3_act]
DONATE BEFORE END-OF-YEAR [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251230_resolution_eoy3_act]
Thank you,
— Cori

As a Congresswoman, she has always shown up when it’s hardest: securing disaster relief, lowering insulin costs, and delivering millions for our communities.
Across St. Louis, families are being priced out and pushed out. Cori Bush is fighting back for affordable housing, fair wages, and utilities as a human right. Be part of this people-first movement. Visit CoriBush.org [https://www.coribush.org] to learn more.

I know it sometimes feels like we’re fighting the Trump administration on so many fronts that we can’t possibly keep track. But there are three major fights that I’m focused on right now:
1. Securing accessible, affordable healthcare for every family in my district and across the country.
2. Defending our veterans and ensuring they receive the support and care they’ve earned.
3. Holding Trump and his corrupt cronies like RFK, Jr. accountable for the lies they spread and the damage they cause.

I’m determined to keep up those fights in Congress.
**But there’s no sugarcoating it: this race is going to be a dogfight.** Here are three reasons I’m still concerned:
1. **Trump gained 13 points** in CA-25 between 2020 and 2024 — and if Republicans flip this seat, it’ll be a big step backward in our push to take back the House in 2026.
2. **Three counties in our district flipped red in 2024,** and Democrats are particularly losing ground in the Inland Empire.
3. **Turnout in CA-25 was alarmingly low** in our special election to pass Prop 50.

**We urgently need to reverse these trends if we’re going to keep our district blue and play our part in flipping the House next year. That starts with Wednesday’s FEC deadline.**

name: Ro Khanna
subject: I stood up to billionaires. Now they’re coming after me.
body:
Billionaires don’t like being asked to pay their fair share. I need you with me.
#
**FIRST:** I stood up for working people and said billionaires should pay a modest 1% tax to help fund healthcare — especially as Republicans gut Medicaid.
**NOW:** Billionaires are openly threatening to bankroll a primary challenger against me because of it.
**Let me be clear: I will not back down from taxing the ultra-wealthy to protect healthcare for millions of Americans.**
But the attacks are real. And they’re escalating.
Billionaires and their allies are furious that I’ve said the quiet part out loud: in the richest country in the world, we shouldn’t be cutting healthcare for working families while billionaires pay a lower effective tax rate than teachers and firefighters.
**[Before I explain more, will you rush a $5 donation to my campaign to help show these billionaires that threatening me will only strengthen our movement?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22144?amount=5&t=1&akid=1430%2E2118727%2E9vyPQN)**
Here’s what they are saying:
[****](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22144?t=2&akid=1430%2E2118727%2E9vyPQN)
**I don’t take PAC money.**
**I don’t take corporate lobbyist money.**
**I don’t take corporate money.**
**My campaign is powered by people like _you_.** And that’s exactly why they want me out of Congress.
This fight isn’t just about me. It’s about whether someone can stand up to tech billionaires while being a representative from Silicon Valley.
If I lose this seat, it sends a message that billionaires can silence anyone who fights for the working class.
**If we win, it proves something powerful: that people power can beat big money – even when they come for us.**
I really need your back right now for the fight that is about to come.
[**Chip in whatever you can today and help us show these billionaires that my seat isn’t for sale.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22144?t=3&akid=1430%2E2118727%2E9vyPQN)
**[DONATE ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22144?amount=5&t=4&akid=1430%2E2118727%2E9vyPQN)**

Thank you for standing with me.
In solidarity,
Ro

body:

Peter,
Tomorrow -- December 31st, New Year’s Eve -- is our latest major fundraising deadline and the latest test for our reelection campaign.
**[That’s why I’m asking for your support at this critical moment. Can you chip in?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20251230-2.9l7erW&refcode=em-20251230-2&t=2&akid=1138%2E1086043%2EHmg7Qy)**

We need to double down now, when times seem toughest, so we can protect our hard-fought progress.
Folks like you power everything we do. If you’ve been waiting for a time to step up and make a donation, this is the time.
Here’s why: Just a few days after this fundraising deadline, Maryland’s fundraising freeze starts. The grassroots donations that come in now will have to power three months of campaigning. That’s why I hope you can step up for the first time before it’s too late.

# Silicon Valley erupts against Khanna endorsement of a Cali wealth tax
Democratic Rep. Ro Khanna, a longtime Silicon Valley ally and architect of major tech-boosting legislation, is **[facing fierce backlash from prominent venture capitalists](https://substack.com/redirect/dbebb571-46c6-4704-9125-550960da1b97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and entrepreneurs after endorsing a proposed California wealth tax targeting billionaires to fund health care.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dbebb571-46c6-4704-9125-550960da1b97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Tech leaders threaten exodus** : Investors like Vinod Khosla warn top talent will flee California if the tax on unrealized gains passes, harming the state's innovation ecosystem.
* **Venture capitalists turn hostile** : Figures including Andreessen Horowitz's Martin Casado and Y Combinator's Garry Tan vow to oppose Khanna politically, with calls to "primary him" or vote him out.
* **Khanna defends modest approach** : The congressman advocates exemptions for startup founders with illiquid stock and dismisses exodus threats as defying economic sense, echoing FDR's quip about missing departing wealthy.
* **Broader Democratic tensions rise** : While national polls show strong support for taxing the rich, California Gov. Gavin Newsom calls state-level billionaire taxes impractical amid growing Republican inroads in tech circles.

* **Outage reports surge** : Over 6,500 users flagged issues on Downdetector shortly after 7 a.m. ET, with most problems tied to the app.
* **Broader services hit** : Disruption extended to Sam's Club site and delayed Walmart deliveries via Amazon's Spark Driver platform.
* **Resolution brings relief** : Walmart's online platforms returned after nearly two hours, restoring access for frustrated shoppers.
* **Company stays silent** : Walmart declined to comment on the cause or details of the technical failure.

* * *
* * *
# Arkansas ticket snags $1.8B Christmas jackpot
A single Powerball ticket **[sold at a gas station in Cabot, Arkansas,](https://substack.com/redirect/b9c3e730-4968-4f58-ab34-e6f615a6b99e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** matched all six numbers in the Christmas Eve drawing Wednesday, claiming a staggering $1.817 billion jackpot -- the second-largest in U.S. lottery history.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b9c3e730-4968-4f58-ab34-e6f615a6b99e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Second-Largest Prize** : This $1.817 billion win trails only the $2.04 billion jackpot claimed in California in 2022, with a cash option of $834.9 million before taxes.
* **Rare Arkansas Victory** : It marks just the second Powerball jackpot ever sold in Arkansas, the first occurring back in 2010.
* **Prize Payment Choices** : Winner can select annuity with one immediate payment plus 29 escalating annual installments or a lump-sum payout of $834.9 million.
* **Slim Winning Odds** : Chances of hitting the jackpot stood at 1 in 292.2 million, ending a lengthy rollover streak since the last win in September.

* * *
* * *
# Samuel Adams Unleashes 30% Beer Banned in 15 States
Boston Beer Company's Samuel Adams **[has released Utopias 2025,](https://substack.com/redirect/d2b87801-4d51-40df-bef5-b4a0bd60eec5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a barrel-aged brew boasting a staggering 30% alcohol by volume -- so potent it's banned for sale in 15 states due to laws capping beer strength.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9ad4587c-4039-42bd-8b25-098fc7e4d681?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Extreme Sipping Experience** : Non-carbonated and ruby-black, Utopias offers complex notes of caramel, oak, dried fruit, subtle smoke, and citrus, resembling barrel-aged spirits more than typical beer.
**Limited Collectible Release** : Bottled in 24.5-ounce resealable ceramic containers for 12-24 small servings, it launched in October with a suggested retail price of $240 per bottle.
**State Ban Specifics** : Prohibited in Alabama, Arkansas, Georgia, Idaho, Missouri, Mississippi, Montana, New Hampshire, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Carolina, Utah, Vermont, and West Virginia.
**Health Risk Warnings** : Experts caution that its high ABV can lead to rapid intoxication and alcohol poisoning risks, far exceeding standard beers in a similar pour.
