Peter,

My name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m running for the U.S. Senate in Minnesota.

**I’m a former Navy SEAL who doesn’t beat around the bush.** I’ve put myself in harm's way more times than I can count because I love what this country stands for.

Leadership doesn’t start on the day one is elected; it’s a quality that one learns from a young age - you exercise it, and it develops over time. President Trump personifies it - so does Marco Rubio.

**But Tim Walz?** He lied about his service in the military, resigning in shame so he wouldn’t have to deploy to an active war zone.

That isn’t leadership, it’s cowardice.

**As governor, the Somali community in Minnesota has defrauded taxpayers of hundreds of millions of dollars, including:**

* **$300m** to pay for the therapy of children with autism, who, in fact, didn’t have autism.

* **$250m** stolen from funds meant to feed hungry children.

Friends,
As the year winds down, I want to take a moment to reflect on what we’ve accomplished together in 2025 — because it’s been incredibly impactful.
Well before Donald Trump took office again in January, attorneys general across the country knew exactly what was coming. We prepared for this fight — because our constituents deserved nothing less than our complete readiness.
And as we expected, the Trump administration came out swinging, targeting California on day one. They repeatedly violated the law, trampled on our rights, and tried to dismantle our democracy.
This year was incredibly difficult for communities all over California, and with each new attack, I dug in my heels and fought harder. To protect our freedoms, defend our democracy, and stand up to abuse of power wherever it appeared.
And we didn’t just show up — we won, too. Our “legal hot streak” (as the LA Times called it) showed what we’re capable of when we fight back with the law on our side and Californians standing with us.
I’m so proud of what we’ve achieved this year – here are just some of what we did:
* Filed more than 50 lawsuits against Donald Trump since January , holding him accountable when he broke the law or violated the Constitution.
* Ended the illegal military occupation of Los Angeles — a federal court ordered Trump to stop the unlawful federalization and deployment of California’s National Guard.
* Protected more than $168 billion in federal funding (and counting) — which translates to $33,600 saved for every $1 spent on legal action.
* Safeguarded billions for California schools, healthcare, infrastructure, and research .
* Stopped the dismantling of critical agencies like AmeriCorps and HHS .
* Defended fundamental constitutional rights, including birthright citizenship and the right to vote .
* Protected wind energy development nationwide , defeating Trump’s unlawful attempt to freeze clean energy projects.
We also held big corporations accountable — securing hundreds of millions of dollars for consumers who were harmed by Big Tech, Big Landlord, and Big Pharma. And we defended California communities by prosecuting corrupt corporate landlords, securing felony convictions against fentanyl traffickers, and holding powerful special interests accountable.
That’s what it looks like to fight back — and win.
But if 2025 has taught us anything, it’s this: the onslaught of unconstitutional orders and unlawful funding clawbacks isn’t slowing down.
Which means neither can we. If you believe this work must continue, please consider making a contribution to my re-election campaign before our end-of-year fundraising deadline tomorrow night. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-25?amount=25]

clean_body: [] Friends, As the year winds down, I want to take a moment to reflect on what we’ve accomplished together in 2025 — because it’s been incredibly impactful. Well before Donald Trump took office again in January, attorneys general across the country knew exactly what was coming. We prepared for this fight — because our constituents deserved nothing less than our complete readiness. And as we expected, the Trump administration came out swinging, targeting California on day one. They repeatedly violated the law, trampled on our rights, and tried to dismantle our democracy. This year was incredibly difficult for communities all over California, and with each new attack, I dug in my heels and fought harder. To protect our freedoms, defend our democracy, and stand up to abuse of power wherever it appeared. And we didn’t just show up — we won, too. Our “legal hot streak” (as the LA Times called it) showed what we’re capable of when we fight back with the law on our side and Californians standing with us. I’m so proud of what we’ve achieved this year – here are just some of what we did: Filed more than 50 lawsuits against Donald Trump since January , holding him accountable when he broke the law or violated the Constitution. Ended the illegal military occupation of Los Angeles — a federal court ordered Trump to stop the unlawful federalization and deployment of California’s National Guard. Protected more than $168 billion in federal funding (and counting) — which translates to $33,600 saved for every $1 spent on legal action. Safeguarded billions for California schools, healthcare, infrastructure, and research . Stopped the dismantling of critical agencies like AmeriCorps and HHS . Defended fundamental constitutional rights, including birthright citizenship and the right to vote . * Protected wind energy development nationwide , defeating Trump’s unlawful attempt to freeze clean energy projects. We also held big corporations accountable — securing hundreds of millions of dollars for consumers who were harmed by Big Tech, Big Landlord, and Big Pharma. And we defended California communities by prosecuting corrupt corporate landlords, securing felony convictions against fentanyl traffickers, and holding powerful special interests accountable. That’s what it looks like to fight back — and win. But if 2025 has taught us anything, it’s this: the onslaught of unconstitutional orders and unlawful funding clawbacks isn’t slowing down. Which means neither can we. If you believe this work must continue, please consider making a contribution to my re-election campaign before our end-of-year fundraising deadline tomorrow night. Thanks for being here with me. —Rob [] Rob Bonta Attorney General of California CONTRIBUTE [] To contribute via check, please address to: Rob Bonta for Attorney General 2026 c/o Deane & Company 1700 Tribute Road, Suite 201 Sacramento, CA 95815

Peter Willis,

Almost ten years ago, Bernie Sanders and I launched Our Revolution. Coming
out of Bernie’s 2016 presidential campaign, we shared a bold vision:
mobilize the grassroots in massive numbers, elect working-class champions
up and down the ballot, and build a Democratic Party that puts people
before profits.

Since then, dark money and billionaire power have exploded as secretive
donors pour hundreds of millions into our elections. A handful of
ultra-wealthy oligarchs can buy nonstop ads, shape the news, and pressure
politicians behind closed doors – all while Trump chips away at our
democracy.

As we look to 2026, the battle lines are clearer than ever – and we have a
real opportunity to stop Trump by electing inspiring progressive
candidates and taking control of Congress. We founded Our Revolution to
take this challenge head on, and now, if we’re going to keep building real
power – block by block, ballot by ballot – we need to know you’re with us.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34883?t=1057&amount=22&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&refcode=email-20251230nd&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=10026%2E5885482%2EWbVuMm ]Will you chip in right now so Our Revolution can take on Trump and his
oligarchs – and win – in 2026?

If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation to Our Revolution will process immediately.

Since our founding, together we’ve delivered some unbelievable victories:

* We’ve elected over 1,000 progressive champions who share our
movement’s values – from Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Zhoran Mamdani
in New York to Ilhan Omar in Minnesota.
* Our pressure helped move the Democratic National Committee to strip
superdelegates’ power from the first round of the presidential
nomination, giving grassroots voters – not party insiders – the final
say.
* Thanks to our organizing, the DNC just pledged to keep corporate and
dark money out of the 2028 presidential primary – a direct blow to the
billionaires and oligarchs desperate to seize even more power.

We’re nowhere near done yet. We’re still pushing to get dark and corporate
money out of all Democratic primaries because we know that until we do,
oligarchs will keep buying our elections and putting in the most
pro-corporate, pro-billionaire candidates they can.

As we speak, Trump’s oligarchs and MAGA billionaires are busy using dark
money to make themselves richer with corporate tax breaks and
mega-government contracts – while slashing the services working families
need to survive. And at the same time, grassroots organizations like ours
are under assault as the far-right puts a target on our back.

The truth is that right now, our work is needed more than ever to seize
the opportunities we have in 2026 to take back power from Trump. Which is
why I’m coming to you today to ask you to fuel the next generation of
people-powered victories so that we’re not just playing defense – we’re
driving the agenda for real progressive change at every level of
government.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34883?t=1054&amount=22&refcode=email-20251230nd&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=10026%2E5885482%2EWbVuMm ]Every dollar that powers Our Revolution is a stake in living wages,
Medicare for All, racial and climate justice, and genuine democracy. Will
you pitch in $8, $27, or whatever you can to fuel Our Revolution through
2026 and into our next decade of impact?

Ten years ago, we started a movement that transformed politics. Today, the
stakes could not be higher: if we let oligarchs continue on the path they
are on, working families, democracy, and our planet will pay the price.
But together, with your help, we will keep organizing – and keep winning.

When we organize, we win,

Larry Cohen

Founding Board Chair, Our Revolution

The Electoral College was a compromise that tired delegates made without truly understanding the future implications. Now we can see the whole system is a disastrous mistake that could lead to the end of true democracy in this country.
This is about stopping anti-democratic forces from using the Electoral College to silence our votes and protect their power. RUSH $25 or more right now and help us erase this poorly designed compromise for good >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=123025_2&amount=25]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
There are times this fight for a popular vote system feels impossible. But friend, we can assure you it's not.
There are a number of ways it can be done. A constitutional amendment, the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (NPVIC), and more.
What we really need is the will to do it -- and that will is growing nationwide. 17 states plus Washington, DC have joined the NPVIC. Those states would likely also pass the amendment to the Constitution.
Momentum is growing as more and more Americans see the need for a popular vote to elect the president. 63% of Americans think the way we elect a president needs to be changed -- a number that's grown over the last decade and is likely higher now than when polled last summer.
Please, help advance the mission to end the Electoral College forever with $25 or more today! >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=123025_2&amount=25]

It’s the biggest tool the opponents of voting rights have to swing national elections and suppress the will of the people. We have to take away this dangerous mechanism that enabled the January 6th insurrection before it happens again.

clean_body: | Hi Peter, As this year comes to a close, I want to talk to you about what’s ahead — because I feel fired up about 2026. In 2025, Democratic pro-choice women delivered real, momentum-building wins. From Miami to Wisconsin to Virginia, we saw expectation-defying performances for our women up and down the ballot. We’ve watched voters’ growing public dissatisfaction with Republican leadership. And we’re hearing from thousands of grassroots Democrats, volunteers, and small-dollar donors who are ready to turn frustration into action. Polling shows it. Special elections show it. I can feel it everywhere I go: people are ready to take back power. After 40 years of building EMILYs List, I’ve learned this lesson well: when voters are angry and energized, we win. And that’s exactly what 2026 offers us. This is why I’m really excited about next year, Peter: we have a real opportunity to take back the U.S. House majority, flip and hold critical U.S. Senate seats, take back power in critical state governments, and elect Democratic pro-choice women at every level who can hold this administration accountable and protect our rights where it matters most. Governors. Attorneys general. Secretaries of state. State legislators and local leaders. These are the women who can block extremist policies, protect access to abortion, defend free and fair elections, and hold the Trump administration accountable when Congress or the courts won't. They are the front line of our democracy — and EMILYs List is already working to recruit, train, and support them. But we cannot do this work without you. Right now, a generous group of grassroots donors has agreed to match every donation made before the end of the year — dollar for dollar — up to $100,000 , for a total end-of-year goal of $200,000. Dear _Flyover_ Reader, I wanted to reach out to you personally as we head into the **final day of 2025**. I know you've seen messages in _The Flyover_ about investing. I know there's a lot of noise everywhere this time of year, so I wanted to slow things down for a moment and speak to you directly. Here's why this moment matters. **1) Time Is Almost Up** We are now **one day away from the end of the year**. Our current investment round is scheduled to **close next month** , and once it does, this opportunity will be gone. If you've been on the sidelines -- thinking about it, meaning to act, waiting for the right moment -- the calendar is giving us that moment right now. One day left in 2025.
One last chance to decide before the year turns. [**Invest in _The Flyover_ today** ](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskcGOmzAQhp_G3BLZY8Bw8KEq5Zamh0pVT5ZjD8GVsREMifL2FbuJ9rLHPY6-mU_z6_9zMicbYkjXn3ZCTUM2Hn1wltCbhPc1IhEuJif09hFxoJCAQ2VnXNacbDT7dBBwkNx874ctxo97URdeD4iAskAtVK0EiJJXxaibhpel81gr2VrVVBdsvQfXOqUaJ1tfBL2LBUguWi4Bjo7DRbiLBMvFoCywkqMPlJfjvxwSjTjER77hcnR5KqIeieaVyW8MegZ9SDdc6ZPNHct-o8mseVscMtl1r_8Z1DuY0IdtYrI73xP6wwl9sE_k7DTbcE1Mdv278wVyIkzEZPfj_PfXto7yCQiXXfW7P3dmDwdVsWg_30OMYa0VK_l1siG-haCvr-Om4X8AAAD__2dEpzk)
* * *
**2) Bonus Shares Are Expiring** As part of our end-of-year push, investors right now receive:
* **15% bonus shares**
* **Even more for larger investments**

These bonus shares are temporary and will expire in just a few days. Once they're gone, they won't be extended. If you've been considering ownership, these are the **most favorable terms** we're offering before this round closes. [**Secure your bonus shares here**](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskcGOmzAQhp_G3BLZY8Bw8KEq5Zamh0pVT5ZjD8GVsREMifL2FbuJ9rLHPY6-mU_z6_9zMicbYkjXn3ZCTUM2Hn1wltCbhPc1IhEuJif09hFxoJCAQ2VnXNacbDT7dBBwkNx874ctxo97URdeD4iAskAtVK0EiJJXxaibhpel81gr2VrVVBdsvQfXOqUaJ1tfBL2LBUguWi4Bjo7DRbiLBMvFoCywkqMPlJfjvxwSjTjER77hcnR5KqIeieaVyW8MegZ9SDdc6ZPNHct-o8mseVscMtl1r_8Z1DuY0IdtYrI73xP6wwl9sE_k7DTbcE1Mdv278wVyIkzEZPfj_PfXto7yCQiXXfW7P3dmDwdVsWg_30OMYa0VK_l1siG-haCvr-Om4X8AAAD__2dEpzk)
* * *
**3) If Not You -- Then Who?** There's a quote often attributed to Edmund Burke: _" The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing."_ Legacy media didn't fail overnight. It failed because too many outlets chased clicks, outrage, and political agendas instead of facts and common sense. And too many good people tuned out, assuming someone else would fix it. The Flyover exists because we chose a different path:
* Facts over spin
* Reporting over celebrity "journalism"
* Common sense over political agendas

But better journalism doesn't survive on good intentions alone. It survives because readers step forward -- not just to read, but to **build and own** something better. As 2025 comes to a close, this isn't a moment for "someday." It's a moment for action. If you believe Americans deserve a better way to consume the news...
If you believe truth still matters...
If you believe doing nothing is no longer an option... [**Become an owner. This round closes next month.
Now is the moment. Warm regards,

clean_body: Why this final day matters more than you might think. | | | | | Dear Flyover Reader, I wanted to reach out to you personally as we head into the final day of 2025. I know you've seen messages in The Flyover about investing. I know there's a lot of noise everywhere this time of year, so I wanted to slow things down for a moment and speak to you directly. Here's why this moment matters. 1) Time Is Almost Up We are now one day away from the end of the year. Our current investment round is scheduled to close next month , and once it does, this opportunity will be gone. If you've been on the sidelines -- thinking about it, meaning to act, waiting for the right moment -- the calendar is giving us that moment right now. One day left in 2025. One last chance to decide before the year turns. 2) Bonus Shares Are Expiring As part of our end-of-year push, investors right now receive: 15% bonus shares Even more for larger investments These bonus shares are temporary and will expire in just a few days. Once they're gone, they won't be extended. If you've been considering ownership, these are the most favorable terms we're offering before this round closes. 3) If Not You -- Then Who? There's a quote often attributed to Edmund Burke: " The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing." Legacy media didn't fail overnight. It failed because too many outlets chased clicks, outrage, and political agendas instead of facts and common sense. And too many good people tuned out, assuming someone else would fix it. The Flyover exists because we chose a different path: Facts over spin Reporting over celebrity "journalism" Common sense over political agendas But better journalism doesn't survive on good intentions alone. It survives because readers step forward -- not just to read, but to build and own something better. As 2025 comes to a close, this isn't a moment for "someday." It's a moment for action. If you believe Americans deserve a better way to consume the news... If you believe truth still matters... If you believe doing nothing is no longer an option... One day left in 2025. This round closes next month. Now is the moment. Warm regards, Cole CEO, The Flyover P.S. We are genuinely grateful for every reader who believes in what we're building. subject: help me celebrate my birthday!
body:
Join us for The Bounce Beat Gala in Greenbelt | | |
---
| | [](https://v8k6.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=69542207bb04c852a997efd1&u=https%3A%2F%2Fkfordjr.com%2Fbdaytickets&w=621a637cd079466c7b27a083&c=b_6953dbd862aaac60070c5927&l=en-US&s=E-Jmie3Fdx5rRanavXuXbiJ-J88%3D)

**Good morning,** As my birthday approaches, this moment feels bigger than a personal milestone – it is a chance to celebrate **our** community, our culture, and the progress we are building together. From the bounce beat that moves our region to the small businesses, families, and organizers who keep our neighborhoods thriving, this campaign is rooted in the stories and strength of people like you.This year, I am inviting you to celebrate with me this Saturday evening at [**The Bounce Beat Gala**](https://v8k6.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=69542207bb04c852a997efd1&u=https%3A%2F%2Fkfordjr.com%2Fbdaytickets&w=621a637cd079466c7b27a083&c=b_6953dbd862aaac60070c5927&l=en-US&s=E-Jmie3Fdx5rRanavXuXbiJ-J88%3D), a black tie optional event that will bring our community together for an elevated night of music, connection, and purpose. Your first and most impactful way to support is by purchasing tickets, tables, or a sponsorship at [**kfordjr.com/bdaytickets**](https://v8k6.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=69542207bb04c852a997efd1&u=https%3A%2F%2Fkfordjr.com%2Fbdaytickets&w=621a637cd079466c7b27a083&c=b_6953dbd862aaac60070c5927&l=en-US&s=E-Jmie3Fdx5rRanavXuXbiJ-J88%3D) and joining us in person.[If you are unable to attend, you can still be part of this moment by making a contribution of $25, $50, $100, or any amount to join my Birthday Donor Circle and help fuel our outreach and voter engagement.](https://v8k6.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=69542207bb04c852a997efd1&u=https%3A%2F%2Fkfordjr.com%2Fbdaytickets&w=621a637cd079466c7b27a083&c=b_6953dbd862aaac60070c5927&l=en-US&s=E-Jmie3Fdx5rRanavXuXbiJ-J88%3D) Members of the Birthday Donor Circle will be recognized as key supporters helping to power this campaign forward in the months ahead.This campaign is about all of us — our triumphs, our struggles, and our shared belief in what’s possible when we come together with purpose and move forward with future generations in mind. I’m honored to be in this with you. _Let’s move District 24, Prince George’s County and Maryland forward._ Together, we can build a future where our community is safer, stronger, and more prosperous — but it will take all of us stepping up, speaking out, and showing up.With gratitude,

[**Kevin Ford Jr.**](https://v8k6.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=69542207bb04c852a997efd1&u=https%3A%2F%2Fkfordjr.com%2Fmeetkford&w=621a637cd079466c7b27a083&c=b_6953dbd862aaac60070c5927&l=en-US&s=gYJhCPBS66cA9LnPa8QU2AdhJrU%3D)

Peter,

There is no easy way to sum up this year in the fight for reproductive rights in the United States. It was a pivotal year, characterized by both devastating setbacks and moments of powerful resistance. Together, we saw the good, the bad, and the downright ugly.

Help us fight back in 2026 and make it a year with more 'GOOD.' [Make your gift to the Center before 12/31 and it will be matched TEN TIMES to help us defend and expand reproductive freedom.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/122287779/592139584/1141910609?sourceid=1151055&utm_campaign=26emjge-1217aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=thegood&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZWNjYjRlMC1iM2U1LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TOmG7aizccQjY_yIi65Z5a2qxL5h70iinD4UXRWfNMA=&emci=e61599b1-6fdf-f011-8194-000d3a1ec8c6&emdi=8eccb4e0-b3e5-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=954237)
> **The Good:** "It's a relief to no longer have to turn away patients from essential health care." – _Long-time Center client in Arizona, Dr. Paul Isaacson, M.D. of the Family Planning Associates Medical Group_
Courts in Arizona and Michigan issued major decisions that removed key barriers to abortion access—including a ban in Arizona that previously criminalized virtually all abortion care after 15 weeks. These victories honored the will of voters who passed constitutional protections for abortion rights. [**GIVE TO FIGHT ABORTION BANS 10X ≫**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/122287781/592139586/1141910609?sourceid=1151055&utm_campaign=26emjge-1217aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=thegood&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZWNjYjRlMC1iM2U1LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TOmG7aizccQjY_yIi65Z5a2qxL5h70iinD4UXRWfNMA=&emci=e61599b1-6fdf-f011-8194-000d3a1ec8c6&emdi=8eccb4e0-b3e5-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=954237)
> **The Bad:** Anti-abortion centers—often called crisis pregnancy centers (CPCs)—have rapidly expanded since _Roe v. Wade_ was overturned, while access to real abortion clinics has shrunk. Today, there are more than 2,600 CPCs nationwide and only 765 abortion clinics.
CPCs masquerade as medical clinics to mislead patients and dissuade them from getting abortions. Despite their deceptive appearance, CPCs are not medical facilities. Many operate without licensed medical staff, are not required to follow HIPAA, and face little regulation—putting patients' privacy and safety at risk. [**GIVE TO PROTECT ABORTION CLINICS 10X ≫**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/122287784/592139588/1141910609?sourceid=1151055&utm_campaign=26emjge-1217aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=thegood&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZWNjYjRlMC1iM2U1LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TOmG7aizccQjY_yIi65Z5a2qxL5h70iinD4UXRWfNMA=&emci=e61599b1-6fdf-f011-8194-000d3a1ec8c6&emdi=8eccb4e0-b3e5-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=954237)
> **The Ugly:** Women are dying because of Texas' abortion bans—while the state continues to escalate attacks on reproductive health care.
Even though Texas' abortion bans claim to allow abortion care for "life-threatening" conditions, extreme penalties have created a climate of fear that prevents doctors from acting. A new Texas law, House Bill 7 (HB7), allows private citizens to sue anyone who allegedly manufactures, distributes, mails, or prescribes abortion pills into Texas—the last remaining lifeline for many Texans who cannot travel out of state to access the abortion care they need.

[This is cruelty by design, and it is why we will never stop fighting abortion bans and restrictions in Texas and across the country.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/122287791/592139594/1141910609?sourceid=1151055&utm_campaign=26emjge-1217aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=thegood&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZWNjYjRlMC1iM2U1LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TOmG7aizccQjY_yIi65Z5a2qxL5h70iinD4UXRWfNMA=&emci=e61599b1-6fdf-f011-8194-000d3a1ec8c6&emdi=8eccb4e0-b3e5-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=954237) [**GIVE TO PROTECT ESSENTIAL HEALTH CARE 10X ≫**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/122287798/592139601/1141910609?sourceid=1151055&utm_campaign=26emjge-1217aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=thegood&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4ZWNjYjRlMC1iM2U1LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TOmG7aizccQjY_yIi65Z5a2qxL5h70iinD4UXRWfNMA=&emci=e61599b1-6fdf-f011-8194-000d3a1ec8c6&emdi=8eccb4e0-b3e5-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=954237) This is our moment. The Bad: Anti-abortion centers—often called crisis pregnancy centers (CPCs)—have rapidly expanded since Roe v. Wade was overturned, while access to real abortion clinics has shrunk. Today, there are more than 2,600 CPCs nationwide and only 765 abortion clinics. CPCs masquerade as medical clinics to mislead patients and dissuade them from getting abortions. Despite their deceptive appearance, CPCs are not medical facilities. Many operate without licensed medical staff, are not required to follow HIPAA, and face little regulation—putting patients' privacy and safety at risk. The Ugly: Women are dying because of Texas' abortion bans—while the state continues to escalate attacks on reproductive health care. Even though Texas' abortion bans claim to allow abortion care for "life-threatening" conditions, extreme penalties have created a climate of fear that prevents doctors from acting. A new Texas law, House Bill 7 (HB7), allows private citizens to sue anyone who allegedly manufactures, distributes, mails, or prescribes abortion pills into Texas—the last remaining lifeline for many Texans who cannot travel out of state to access the abortion care they need. This is our moment. Together, we will end bans, remove barriers, and protect what matters most—reproductive freedom. We love taking a moment to reflect on the year behind us—and tomorrow’s newsletter will do just that. It’ll be fully dedicated to 2025, with a rewind of the year’s biggest stories, moments, and headlines that shaped Colorado and beyond. Stay tuned and in the meantime, check out our top 2025 stories below or [click here](https://link.email.joinrmv.)!
Listen to today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Immigration, wildlife policy, and labor unrest dominated headlines as a proposed 2026 ballot initiative would force local law enforcement to cooperate with ICE, setting up a [major fight over sanctuary policies](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Rural tensions flared as county commissioners urged Gov. Polis to [pause gray wolf relocations](https://link.email.joinrmv.) and ag groups clashed with activists over [coyote management](https://link.email.joinrmv.). In Telluride, a [holiday-season labor dispute](https://link.email.joinrmv.) shut down ski patrol operations, leaving slopes empty and small mountain businesses reeling.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** National attention turned to accountability after a [YouTuber exposed large-scale Somali-linked fraud](https://link.email.joinrmv.) in Minnesota largely missed by legacy media, while a year-end review of the Left’s [“Top 25 Lies of 2025”](https://link.email.joinrmv.) argued misinformation shaped major debates on immigration, elections, energy, and public safety.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** A look back at [RMV’s most-read stories of 2025](https://link.email.joinrmv.) shows readers stuck with reporting grounded in documents, data, and follow-through—rewarding accountability journalism that tested power, tracked consequences, and stayed focused on facts over noise.
This is your Mountain Minute for December 30, 2025.

This list wasn’t built in a meeting. It formed over time, story by story, as readers decided what was worth stopping for.
What follows are the 25 RMV stories that held attention in 2025—and didn’t let go.
The 25 stories ranked in this piece reflect what Colorado readers chose to spend time with in 2025. This list was not assembled through editorial preference or hindsight. It is shaped by reader engagement over the course of the year and, taken together, it offers a picture of what held attention and why.
Across the list, one pattern surfaced quickly. Readers did not gravitate toward reaction for its own sake. They stayed with reporting that showed its work, followed the record, and traced consequences.

**[Colorado Voters Could Decide Future Of ICE And Local Law Enforcement Cooperation](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** [DENVER7](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Voters could rein in Colorado’s sanctuary-style laws:** The proposed 2026 ballot initiative would require local law enforcement to notify federal authorities when individuals who are not lawfully present are charged with violent crimes or are repeat felons, directly challenging Colorado’s current restrictions on ICE cooperation and restoring a commonsense public-safety standard.
* **Measure targets dangerous offenders—not routine arrests:** Backers emphasize the language is narrowly written, triggered only at the charging stage by prosecutors, countering claims of overreach and reinforcing that the focus is violent criminals and repeat felony offenders, not law-abiding residents or minor offenses.
* **A direct response to laws that tie officers’ hands:** Supporters argue Colorado’s existing policies—and new penalties for sharing immigration data—have gone too far, undermining public safety and voter intent, and say the initiative restores balance by prioritizing victims’ rights and community safety over ideological resistance to federal enforcement .

**[Federal Eyes Turn to Minnesota After YouTuber Exposes Massive Childcare Fraud](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** [TOWNHALL](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Independent journalists exposed massive fraud the media ignored:** YouTuber Nick Shirley documented empty daycare centers in Minnesota collecting millions in public funds, uncovering what federal officials now describe as widespread Somali-linked fraud schemes spanning childcare, Medicare, and other programs—while legacy media largely stayed silent.
* **State leadership allowed abuse to flourish unchecked:** The article argues Gov. Tim Walz’s administration failed to stop or seriously investigate the schemes despite years of warning signs, forcing federal authorities to step in after billions in taxpayer dollars were allegedly siphoned off.
* **Media bias and weak oversight put taxpayers at risk:** The piece highlights how ideological blind spots and fear of political backlash led major outlets to downplay or delay coverage, reinforcing conservative concerns that lax enforcement and activist journalism enable large-scale fraud against American taxpayers.

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter, do you know
what these eight progressive candidates have in common? ⤵️

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251230.p3XgLk&refcode=em20251230-37326&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37326%2E1203867%2EPB2Rpm ]A graphic titled 'Upcoming Elections' displays photos and information
for eight Justice Democrats candidates in upcoming 2026 Democratic
primaries. Each candidate has a labeled “Upcoming Primary” banner, name,
district, and two pink buttons for “Website” and “Donate.” The candidates
shown are: Angela Gonzales-Torres (CA-34), Melat Kiros (CO-01), Junaid
Ahmed (IL-08), Donavan McKinney (MI-13), Cori Bush (MO-01), Nida Allam
(NC-04), Darializa Avila Chevalier (NY-13), and Justin J. Pearson (TN-09).

These eight young, working-class fighters have all been endorsed by
Justice Democrats this year. They’re all going up against out-of-touch,
Do-Nothing corporate Democrats who’ve upheld the status quo for too long.

And they’re not taking a dime from AIPAC, the Crypto lobby, or corporate
PACs.

And that’s why they’re all relying on you to help them go toe-to-toe with
AIPAC and AI Big Tech billionaires who are lining up to pour millions of
dollars of corporate money into their races.

Poll after poll tells us that Democratic voters are ready to elect a new
generation of progressive changemakers. But far too often, true
progressives don’t make it onto the ballot in the general election because
they don’t have enough money or resources to compete with the
corporate-backed Democratic establishment.

*This* is the exact reason why our organization was
created, Peter: to connect
grassroots supporters with bold, new candidates challenging the
establishment in Democratic primaries.

Justice Democrats exists to fundamentally change this broken dynamic in
our political system. And this team has shown that progressive change is
possible when we stand up and demand it together.

Our eight new candidates will only succeed if they receive enough support

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). | **Dear Kansan,**

As we come to the close of the year, I want to thank you for the trust you place in me and take a moment to reflect on what we’ve accomplished together in 2025 — and where we’re headed next.

This past year brought real challenges for our country, but it also delivered meaningful progress. In Congress, Republicans stayed focused on standing up for Kansas values and pushing back against policies that weren’t working for families, farmers, and communities across our state.

**In 2025, we fought for and delivered real results,** including:
* Taking action to **strengthen border security** and hold the Biden administration accountable for failed open-border policies.
* Working to **rein in reckless federal spending** and push back against inflation that has strained family budgets.
* Standing up for parents’ rights and **protecting children** from radical policies
* **Supporting Kansas agriculture, rural communities, and local job creators.**
* D**efending constitutional freedoms** and commonsense conservative principles.

While there is more work to be done, these efforts matter — and they’re making a difference for Kansans.

As we look ahead to 2026, I’m optimistic about what we can accomplish together. The year ahead presents an opportunity to build on this momentum and continue delivering results.

**In 2026, our focus will remain on:**
* **Securing the border** and stopping fentanyl and human trafficking.
* Promoting fiscal responsibility and **reducing Washington’s runaway spending.**
* Strengthening our economy and **lowering costs for Kansas families.**
* **Standing firm for parents** , faith, and freedom.
* **Ensuring government works for the people** — not against them.

My commitment is simple: to listen to Kansans, fight for conservative solutions, and never lose sight of who I serve. I’m grateful for your engagement and support, and I look forward to continuing this work in the year ahead.

As we prepare to welcome a new year, I wish you and your family a prosperous and blessed New Year.

**Yours in the fight,**

Tracey Mann

As we prepare to close the book on 2025, we’ve been doing a lot of reflecting.
We faced a political landscape that tested our resolve and forced us to fight harder than ever for our values. Here in Pennsylvania, we didn't just hold the line, we pushed back. We have so much to be proud of. Because you showed up and helped with donations and with your time, we:

Folks – it’s Ben, John’s finance director.

I made a tough call this week.

In a Team Fetterman meeting, it became clear that with a little more money, we could take a real fight to Republicans in the 2026 midterms. The problem? The money isn’t in the budget. Not yet.

I gave the green light anyway – counting on us hitting our end-of-year goal. It’s a risk. But this is the moment to take one.

We can’t underinvest right as we hit the midterm election cycle. That would be a mistake.

The bet I’m making is simple: if folks understand what’s at stake in 2026, they’ll step up to close the gap. I’m hoping you will.

So folks, here's my ask: Will you chip in $5 to help us meet our crucial $50,000 end-of-year goal? It’s contributions from folks like you that are going to make all the difference.

body:

Dear Peter,
When the world feels uncertain, I find strength in knowing that every redwood project at Save the Redwoods is rooted in science, unlocking opportunities for how we work and collaborate in redwood forests.
From studying how fire shapes the land to mapping the elements of climate-resilient forests, our work turns decades of research into bold solutions for the future.
As 2025 comes to a close, you can triple your impact [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-rrf-3] thanks to a generous, additional match from the Troper Wojcicki Foundation. Your gift to the Redwood Resilience Fund will power our science-based practices for stewarding the forests of the future.
TRIPLE YOUR GIFT [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-rrf-3] [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-rrf-3]
Our science team has developed a new conservation planning tool that identifies where redwood trees are most vulnerable and where protection will have the greatest benefit for biodiversity, climate resilience, and community access. Every acre we protect strengthens the forest for generations to come.
If you’ve been waiting for the right time to give, this is it. Your first gift will be tripled to protect the redwood forests through science-based conservation.Give to the Redwood Resilience Fund, and your support will go 3x as far! [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-rrf-3]
Through continued science-based decision making and support from forest stewards like you, we can ensure that redwood forests have greater resilience now and in the future.

* * *
_**by Cliff Schecter**_
Mamdani vs Musk seems to be on, and by God, it's difficult picking sides!
Per usual, Elon can't shut his colossal, constant, pablum-emitting-cake-hole. The Ketamine Kid _likes_ to ratchet up Russian disinformation while bullying any non-single-cell organism on the (dis)information platform he bought and renamed X.
Ya know, because of all the similarities to Malcolm X.
So you have Elon, the fungus-y yacht-kateer with a mind by K-hole, body by Newt Gingrich. A guy who can only gain vast wealth in a country where we reward Dunning-Kruger, audacious shamelessness, and an emotional IQ best described as _AI in heat_.
Meanwhile, Mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani has proposed a number of far-reaching proposals for New York. Like a rent stabilization freeze, as rents have skyrocketed under the Trump economic "plan." I'm told it's Bolshevik by @MAGALOVE483567433 on Twitter.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de60e783-f8b5-4679-86e7-59c688182a49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Makes sense, as the New York City Rent Stabilization Law of 1969 passed while Republican Richard Nixon was President, Republican Nelson Rockefeller--of the Commie lineage!--was NY Governor, and Republican John Lindsey was NYC Mayor.
This is a crucial affordability issue. Mamdani is also trying to tackle that with other proposals, like free public transportation. Would this help millions of people now struggling under Trump's stagflation? Yes.
Can it work? I dunno. But it seems to in Luxembourg, Malta, and Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. And, hell, we tried supply-side economics, mapped out a barroom napkin--true story! So, I think we can give free public transportation a shot, see if studies that show it raises productivity, more people enter the workforce, etc., are accurate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de60e783-f8b5-4679-86e7-59c688182a49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The rigorous study that created an economic theory that ended up bankrupting us_
* * *
Some of Mamdani's ideas won't pass go, some'll be flushed out but not make it (there's the city council he has to contend with, and in NY the Governor, due to some quirky laws, has say in many city economic matters).
But some common-sense measures, due to our insane income inequality, will pass. And likely make some lives better. And the Overton Window will expand faster than a shirtless Musk on a yacht (guess nobody in the vicinity had an itchy harpoon finger).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de60e783-f8b5-4679-86e7-59c688182a49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Elon Musk shows off one of his patented "Dudley Moore is drunk in a film again" looks_
* * *
I think I prefer that vision to the guy who bought into PayPal with mommy and daddy's emerald mine money. What a genius, being born to that mom and dad! His ideas and coding sucked, but who's gonna hold down another rich prat with high self-regard using family booty to buy ideas?
Then he did that thing he hates when anyone of a different race, sexual orientation, or their original chin does it: _He got the government to pay for his company to grow._
He's also a vandal who broke into our Treasury Department with "Big Balls" and the crew without the credentials of an actual task force, accessing data he had no legal right to go near. He settled a sexual harassment suit at SpaceX.
_Made Shanghai Tesla workers live and sleep on the factory floor for days to meet production quotas._
* * *

* * *
And maybe his most special contribution: he destroyed USAID, which included erasing 20,000 jobs, wrecking a key part of our soft-power national security, and **killing 500K-700K people living in developing countries,**_**including over 200,000 children.**_(_**Center for Global Development**_).
So when Elon attacked a Mamdani appointee for her "lack of experience," the corrugated ass-canoe with the government experience of a wombat is on weaker ground than a SpaceX terminal after its regularly scheduled explosion during take off.
But he did it anyhow, slamming Mamdani's **commissioner of the Fire Department of New York (FDNY)** nominee, Lillian Bonsignore, on his dumbed-down social media platform. The fire expert, via osmosis, warned that appointing someone lacking traditional firefighting experience meant "people will die."
Insert eyes-rolling emoji.
Bonsignore has worked at FDNY for 31 years and led the department's Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Division. The place where 70% of the calls come in for emergencies.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de60e783-f8b5-4679-86e7-59c688182a49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So if you think Elon sound a bit sus, you'd be right. Because guess what else Bonsignore is--no, not one of Elon's kids, though with 412 out there, I get it's a statistically valid inquiry. No, it turns out _**Bonsignore is the second woman and first openly gay FDNY commissioner-to-be**_. Man, does that piss a Nazi off.
Mamdani responded by pointing out Bonsignore's leadership during 9/11 and the COVID-19 pandemic. Elon didn't lead anything during 9/11 except maybe in incel hair implants
And for the coup de grace, just look at otherworldly stupid crap this supposed smart man of the manosphere shares on Twitter without a second thought (or first):
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de60e783-f8b5-4679-86e7-59c688182a49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Sorry, E-Loan, undocumented workers don't get Social Security. Maybe in your home country, I'm not sure how things work in South Africa. But thanks for sharing!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/da4324af-b44c-4a14-bf77-55cb1fabff7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here we'll see real human beings who didn't live on Elon's segregated side of the tracks get hurt here because of his bullshit. But he doesn't care, he has a Hitler to Heil at a conference somewhere, I'm sure he's later for.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8beb6351-5cad-4e25-b450-3134c05a4817?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Also kudos to Trump's U.S. Dept of Labor for sharing Stalin-level disinformation! ](https://substack.com/redirect/c12f3351-8b85-472a-9e18-9b89daa4e281?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In the end, Democrats should SO want this fight:
**On one side:** A social democratic vision of real democracy, affordability, and an economy for all Americans. Prioritizing a return of privacy, freedom from masked goons, [guaranteed healthcare](https://substack.com/redirect/cefde463-61c6-4526-b7bd-6b0f39825de8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), affordable housing, and family leave-for-all.
**On the other:** A Nazi-loving, crony-capitalist oligarch handed our tax dollars to tank companies and spew vile shit. With an obscene trillion-dollar pay package from pals he installed on the Tesla board. Trump tax cuts and subsidies for malfunctioning cyber trucks stolen from SNAP and Medicaid for sick and starving children
Elon would dry hump Xi's leg for a large order of Cybertrucks. Ya know, the thing that looks like two toasters sexed while mom was on a strict diet of Jim Beam and menthols, and _this_ was their offspring.
The GD thing is so ugly it asks Stephen Miller for dating tips.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de60e783-f8b5-4679-86e7-59c688182a49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
How are people so generally incoherent that they're suckered into buying an aesthetic abomination--a large tin can with panels falling off because of a "brand?" How are they selling, you ask? You'll definitely wanna starve more kids for subsidies:
> **" ...declining new sales, plummeting resale values, and a failure to meet initial high demand projections, driven by high prices (even after discounts), quality issues, recalls, disappointing specs (range/towing), and its polarizing design"**
Wow, money well spent!
Now, let's get back to our regularly scheduled program.[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/032e34b9-3d11-44a0-8647-723f5846f516?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Democratic leaders](https://substack.com/redirect/032e34b9-3d11-44a0-8647-723f5846f516?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[, this is a layup. Create a simple, truthful message with emotional resonance and repeat it, FFS.](https://substack.com/redirect/032e34b9-3d11-44a0-8647-723f5846f516?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) It's called "contrast." Look at a farmer Trump bankrupted (sadly, you have a wide choice) and ask if they want their job or Elon's 11,214th Rolodex? Or a family whose aid ElonTrump cut, and ask "your child eating or Elon's 47th flab-encrusted yacht?
Cancer treatment for your Papa or Elon the plutocrat's private, backroom deals to subsidize his newest stupid concoction, Neuralink, so he can try to steal your thoughts and impulses like he's a Jim Carrey Riddler from Batman
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de60e783-f8b5-4679-86e7-59c688182a49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So Musk's vision vs Mamdani's? Wow, such a toughie!
It's pretty simple: Elon Musk has cost America, and its people more in money, souls, and the soul of America than any boogie-man immigrant he makes up ever could.

As 2025 comes to a close, one reality is becoming increasingly clear: American politics is undergoing a major shift. Latino voters have put affordability as a key issue front and center, and Latino candidates are running for office in numbers this country has never seen before.
In the season finale of the Latino Vote Podcast, hosts Chuck Rocha and Mike Madrid take a wide-ranging look at how the political landscape has changed over the past twelve months, moving beyond polling and into what is actually happening in elections, campaigns, and communities across the country. Their conclusion is unmistakable: Latino voters are no longer a peripheral demographic. They are becoming the deciding force in American politics.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..XjMpYW7e189DcWZ7wzdnHJTFbCayCdMobqufkSWhe2Q?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=182993959)
### Trump's Historic Collapse
Donald Trump is experiencing historic lows in approval ratings--the worst of both his terms. He's losing hardcore MAGA supporters. He's underwater by 25 points on the economy. And most importantly, Latino voters are leading the charge away from him.
Why? Because you can lie to people about foreign aid, you can lie about Ukraine, but you can't lie to them when they go to the grocery store and see that the price of ground beef is through the roof. Or when they suddenly can't afford healthcare. Trump promised an A+++ economy. Instead, he gave us tariffs, chaos, and higher prices on everything.
### The Rise of Latino Candidates Everywhere
What's really exciting is the explosion of Latino candidates across America.
We're not just talking about the usual suspects in California and Texas. We're seeing:
* [Salt Lake City Council Member Eva Lopez Chavez running in Utah's new 1st Congressional District.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c5462456-82a1-4060-90e4-268c977ce410?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* [Political Director of Bernie Sanders' 2020 Presidential Campaign, Analilia Mejia, is running to replace Mikey Sherrill in New Jersey 11th District](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8991457b-27a0-4219-99c7-2d7bf0439c6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* [John Lira, Marine veteran, in Texas's 35th district](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/36d7dfe6-0352-4062-91a2-ce9dd8edd729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* [John Paul Torres in Michigan's 11th congressional district](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1e8135bc-766a-4087-af36-a6fff6ca3444?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* And many, many more.

### Just Look at the Math
Mike Madrid dropped a crucial insight that everyone needs to understand:
_**' Latinos are the only swing voters left in America.'**_
Think about that. While every other demographic has sorted itself into partisan camps, Latinos are swinging back and forth based on performance, issues, and who's actually delivering.
Here's the other number that should keep both parties up at night: Latinos currently turn out at rates about 5-6 points lower than white voters. If we simply matched white turnout--not exceeded it, just matched it--the entire complexion of American politics changes overnight.
### What Rocha and Madrid are Building Together
Chuck and Mike have a vision for 2026 and beyond. They want to create something that Latinos have never had: a coordinated fundraising network that can give Latino candidates across the country a real shot from day one.
Every other community has this. Whether you're Black, Asian, Jewish, Persian, Greek--if you're a woman--there are organizations that will open their checkbooks and give candidates instant credibility and resources. Emily's List for female candidates. Various ethnic community networks for other groups. Etc.
Latinos have never had that. Cuban-Americans in South Florida, maybe. But for the rest of Latinos? Nothing.
Here's the idea: If everyone listening to this podcast gave $10 to support Latino candidates, if we all chipped in where we can, we could create the kind of startup infrastructure that other communities have had for decades.
We don't have billionaire donors. But we have numbers. If we organize our community, even small contributions multiplied across thousands of supporters can create the kind of startup capital that makes campaigns viable.
That's what Chuck and Mike are building. And they need your help.
[Visit our Website](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f9993a08-f706-4d1c-911f-6bd308aa51f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### What You Can Do Right Now
1. **Share this episode** with everyone you know who wants more Latino representation in politics.
2. **Follow candidates** like Eva Lopez Chavez (UT-1) Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), John Paul Torres (MI-11), and John Lira (TX-35).
3. **Send us names** of Latino candidates running in your area - [email us](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fb7d2214-4733-4a12-9d46-069ca936c836?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), DM us, tag us on social media. [Find us on X](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f1a557cc-3f58-4831-8765-85724cc97ded?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [and Bluesky](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/220ec7ed-f3e5-4b95-85bf-006f0c4fe7f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [Comment on our YouTube page](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/390fade3-23b0-4999-ac34-c14a43913976?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
4. **Commit to supporting Latino candidates** , even if it's just $10.
5. **Register to vote** and commit to showing up in 2026. Higher Latino turnout means more politicians will listen to our needs.

From the entire Latino Vote podcast team: **Happy holidays. Hug your parents if you 're lucky enough to have them.** Even make peace with that MAGA uncle--find what you like about him, not what you hate. **Choose love, not hate.**
**2026 is going to be historic. Let 's make sure the Latino community is ready.**

body:
2025 was a big year - and 2026 will be even bigger as we work to flip AZ-06!

| | | | | [|
---](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=00b9cec7b2&e=fea3203902)
| | | | |
---
| |
# THE MENDOZA BRIEF
# The Latest News from Team Mendoza
# 2025 Wrap-up Edition
---
| | The Mendoza Brief is a way for our campaign to share the latest news, opportunities, and updates from the campaign trail. Happy New Year, Arizona! 🏜️
---
| [Fuel Jo’s Mission Today!](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=c8149a66a3&e=fea3203902)
---
|
---
| |
# A Note From Jo
---
| | Friends,
As 2025 comes to a close, I’ve been reflecting on what we’ve accomplished this year. The momentum behind our campaign is real - and it’s growing by the day. Since launching in February, I’ve had the privilege of meeting so many people across Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District. They’ve shared their stories, their struggles, and what they want from a representative in Congress: someone who listens, who leads with integrity, and who never forgets where they came from. People are tired of politicians who forget who they serve the moment they reach Washington.
Our communities are tired of being treated as political pawns by out-of-touch Members of Congress, like Juan Ciscomani. Southern Arizonans deserve stability and respect, not political theater. While Congress stalls, families are forced to stretch every dollar further. Gas, groceries, rent, and utilities are becoming more unaffordable by the day and it’s our most vulnerable neighbors who pay the price. That’s why I’m fighting for solutions rooted in working-class values: affordable health care, good-paying jobs, and real investment in rural and border communities.
I’m proud to say we’ve built a grassroots army of over 55,000 people from across the country who have joined our fight to flip AZ-06. With the endorsements of both of our U.S. Senators and the backing of many powerhouse organizations, we’re laying the groundwork to fire Juan Ciscomani and finally deliver the leadership this district deserves.
It’s no secret that this will be one of the toughest, most expensive races in the country - and we need to be ready. But it’s going to take everything we’ve got. That’s why I’m asking you to join us in the trenches. Sign up to volunteer, sign my petition, contribute if you can, and help spread the word.
We’re coming fast, committed, and strong. Let’s finish the mission - together.
In Service,Jo
---
|
---
|
---

| |
# 2025 Endorsement Roundup
---
| | Since launching her campaign in February, Jo secured support from a vast coalition of local, state, and nationwide leaders and organizations who know that she will be a relentless leader for Southern Arizona in Congress.
These endorsements come with a commitment to put boots on the ground in 2026 to reach as many voters as possible to share Jo’s message. Every effort will be made to let Arizonans know that they have an option to elect someone who will lead with courage and dignity in Washington DC.
The current list of endorsements can be found on Jo’s website, and will continue to be updated as Jo garners more support throughout 2026.

---
|
---
| |
# Rounding out 2025 with Vets for Mendoza!
---
| | Earlier this month, Jo joined Vets for Mendoza for a holiday get-together in support of homeless veterans. She had the chance to connect with veterans and military families and thank them for their support and commitment to helping our communities.
---

|
---
| |
# Help Get Jo on the Ballot!
---
| | The April filing deadline will be here before we know it, and if we’re going to flip AZ-06, we need to get Jo on the ballot first! If you live in AZ-06, you can sign Jo’s petition online below.
---
| [Sign Jo’s petition online!](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=b272022459&e=fea3203902)
---
| | Interested in joining a canvass in your area or circulating a petition yourself? Let us know by filling out the form through the button below or email us at **info@joannamendoza.com**.
---
| [Sign up to volunteer!](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=dfcc5780ea&e=fea3203902)

|
---
| |
# Help Jo Finish the Year Strong
---
| | Jo has built a grassroots movement of over 55,000 supporters across AZ-06 and the country and raised over $2 million since launching her campaign. This campaign is powered by everyday people, with an average contribution of $22.
As 2025 wraps up, so is the final quarter of the year. We must keep the momentum going to ensure we have the resources we need to flip this district in the New Year. Help Jo finish this quarter - and the year - strong by pitching in what you can!
---
| [Help Jo finish 2025 strong!](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=e32b325ac1&e=fea3203902)

# 308 Days Until We Flip AZ-06
---
| | The 2026 general election is **308 days away** \- and Jo is already out in the district, listening and meeting with voters, and laying the groundwork to fight for southern Arizonans in DC. If you have any questions, do not hesitate to reach out. Stay tuned for when Jo will be in a community near you!
Let’s win this thing, Arizona!

name: Chris Pappas
subject: I’m worried about the next 48 hours
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
We’re barreling towards the deadline and I’m worried about a few things.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=4308%2E582294%2EgLy4qM)
I’m worried that what happens in the next 48 hours will determine the narrative of this entire midterm election. And as we barrel towards our end-of-quarter FEC deadline, here’s what I’m ruminating over:
* **We are**** __the__****target for Republicans.** After every single county in New Hampshire shifted toward the Republicans in 2024, the NRSC and billionaire-backed super PACs circled our state as their top pick-up opportunity. They see a path to a hardened Republican majority in the Senate that runs right through our backyards. And they’ve picked an old, familiar name in John Sununu to run against us.
* **We are**** __the__****anti-Trump firewall.** This isn’t just about a seat in the Senate. It’s about standing up to Donald Trump’s extreme agenda in the second half of his term. We cannot afford to lose a single seat if we want to protect our democracy and our way of life.
* **Pundits & PACs __are__ paying attention to this 48-hour deadline. At midnight tomorrow the FEC closes the books on the quarter. Our fundraising numbers will become public under finance law. Every GOP strategist and dark-money group will be scanning the FEC reports looking for a crack in our foundation. A strong report doesn't just fund our campaign — it acts as a psychological shield that can scare off opposing super PACs and donors.**

**If we post a giant fundraising total powered by lots of grassroots donors, we send a clear message that our campaign has momentum. That momentum will get covered by the press. It’ll scare off the NRSC and outside funders.

But if we fall short, we invite an avalanche of Republican money into New Hampshire. They’re going to see us as weak, and they’ll want to strike to take us out.**
**There’s a lot riding on what happens in the next 48 hours.** We set an ambitious fundraising goal for all the aforementioned reasons, and the only way we can get there is if you step up right now to make your first donation before the FEC deadline.
[**Will you chip in $5 before our FEC deadline to send a powerful message to the politicians, pundits, and PACs who are watching? Every dollar helps us show strength and say loudly and clearly:****_We are going to win this election._**](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20251230_3.OIA-A-&amount=5&refcode=em20251230-3&t=2&akid=4308%2E582294%2EgLy4qM)

Running a small business and serving in Congress have both taught me that real success isn't something one person achieves on their own — it happens when a group of people decides to work toward a common goal.
I can't stand up to the millions of dollars the GOP is planning to spend by myself, but this grassroots team can. This isn't just my campaign; it's a movement we're building together. I really need to see us come together over these next 48 hours so we can post a number that shows exactly how strong we are.
I know you all will come through.
With gratitude,
Chris Pappas

name: Roy Cooper
subject: I can’t quite wrap my head around it
body:
He’s wrong for this country.
Peter, it’s almost unimaginable to me that someone could have the privilege of serving this nation in the United States Senate and decide to serve only their political party.
But that’s what we’re seeing of far too many Republicans in Washington. It’s exactly what we’d get from my opponent if he wins this toss-up race.
He’s not running because he believes that Americans deserve loyalty from their elected leaders. He said he’s running because President Trump told him to.
**You just can’t be 100% loyal to the people if you’re 100% loyal to a political party or a president.**
Look, at the end of the day, Michael Whatley would not be a Senator for the people. He’d just be another rubber stamp for the MAGA agenda. He’s wrong for this state and our country. We have to defeat him.
**[We’re one day out from our final end-of-quarter filing deadline of 2025-- the last before our election year begins. We set a $1 million online fundraising goal. It’s high, but since Whatley has big-money donors and PACs lined up to support him, it’s what we need to raise in order to keep up. I’m personally asking if you can get us started on our goal by splitting a donation of any amount now between our campaign and Wes Moore.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20251230-3.yXghS0&refcode=em-20251230-3&t=1&akid=1133%2E1086043%2EDp_Lgq)**
Can’t do this without you,
Roy Cooper

name: Voter Action Project
subject: “There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Voter Action Project[https://voteractionproject.org/]
The Senate is standing up to stop the SAVE Act in its tracks, folks.
Defenders of voting rights know that non-citizen voting is already illegal, extremely rare, and that this bill is written in a way that could disenfranchise millions of eligible women across the country. Here's Colorado Senator Michael Bennet:
(Image of Michael Bennet speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_MB.jpg]
Opponents of voting rights in Congress -- and in the White House -- favor this bill because they know it could suppress millions of eligible voters, changing the composition of the electorate and potentially empowering them and their party for years to come.
Please, Team, join these brave Senators today. Fuel our efforts to stop this dangerous legislation with $25 or whatever you can and ensure millions of women's voices continue to be heard in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=123025_3&amount=25]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=123025_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=123025_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=123025_3&amount=50]
