We know the SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before the next election, folks. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law.
If you missed it: This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. And that’s the point.
The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
The consequences of a bill like this passing would be simply catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $25 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=123025_3&amount=25]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

name: Tobias Read
subject: The Trump administration has repeatedly demanded access to Oregonians’ private voter data.
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251230em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251230em]
I want to be very clear about what’s happening right now — and why the final days of this year matter so much.
The Trump administration has repeatedly demanded access to Oregonians’ private voter data. Dates of birth. Driver’s license numbers. Partial Social Security numbers.
Worst of all, they provided no transparency, legal authority, or explanation for how that data would be used or protected. So I said no.
I said no because protecting voter privacy is part of my job. Because Oregon voters don’t answer to Washington DC bullies. And because once trust in our elections is broken, it’s incredibly hard to rebuild.
But standing up to the Trump Administration won’t end in 2025. In fact, our work is only just getting started.
That’s why it’s so important that we end the year in a strong position — so that we can be prepared for all the fights that 2026 and the years to come bring. Can I count on you to chip in $5, $10, or more right now to help me continue fighting back and standing up for Oregon’s democracy in the face of this lawless administration? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251230em]
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251230em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251230em]
This federal overreach by Donald Trump is not an abstract issue.
We’ve already seen voter data quietly shared between federal agencies, lawsuits filed to intimidate states into compliance, and officials in the administration attempting to scare us into silence.
Their tactics won’t work. But I can’t keep up the fight alone. Grassroots support is what allows us to defend Oregon’s elections, protect vote-by-mail, and keep the public informed when the stakes are high and the pressure is real.
If you’re able, will you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can before our end-of-year deadline to help us meet this goal and head into the new year strong? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251230em]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=251230em]
Oregon has led the nation on secure, accessible elections. With your help, we’ll keep leading — and keep saying no when it matters.
Thank you for standing with me,
Tobias Read

name: Costello for U.S. Senate
subject: Welcoming Rain—and Real Change
body:
As Maine looks for relief from drought, voters are also calling for deep political reform.

| | | | | [|
---](https://costelloforsenate.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d37adbc910a9a40e00b14f5&id=6df51798ac&e=5d7176e969)
| | | | [|
---](https://costelloforsenate.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d37adbc910a9a40e00b14f5&id=f14815c948&e=5d7176e969)
| |

**Welcoming Rain and Change** Friends,As we close out 2025, Mainers are anxious for more than just rain this year (given our historic drought). We Mainers and most Americans desire considerable political and governmental change, and David is the only candidate for the US Senate to detail and promote extensive, long-overdue fixes to our nation’s imperfect democracy and government._Read David’s recent email (below) to the Press Herald’s new politics editor making the case for broader, more substantive press coverage._ Given his working-class roots, bold reform ideas, and extensive senior-level government experience - we continue to believe that David is the best candidate to unseat Senator Collins in 2026 and help in realizing the kind of governmental changes needed to fix Washington and address the needs and concerns of most Mainers (and Americans). Please consider joining us in making the case for real change and supporting David’s efforts to succeed by sharing this email with others and contributing $15, or any amount that works for you, to help in ramping up our campaign activities.Thank you,Team CostelloP.S. For more information on David’s background, experience, and policy positions, visit our Campaign’s website ([costelloforsenate.com.](https://costelloforsenate.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d37adbc910a9a40e00b14f5&id=b03a140dac&e=5d7176e969)) and David’s Facebook page ([https://www.facebook.com/CostelloForMaine](https://costelloforsenate.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d37adbc910a9a40e00b14f5&id=7854ff44ed&e=5d7176e969)). Additionally, for those interested in helping to collect primary ballot signatures please let us know at [campaign@costelloforsenate.com](mailto:campaign@costelloforsenate.com). Our work to collect signatures from 2,000 registered Democrats will run from January to March.
**Email to the new politics editor at the Portland Press Herald:**
Hi Kirby, Welcome to Maine. I’m one of the lesser-known Democrats running for the US Senate, and I’m writing to make a pitch for broader, deeper coverage of the US Senate race in Maine. As you know, the Democratic primary has largely, in the press, been narrowed to a two-person race, even though neither candidate, Graham Platner, nor Governor Mills is a slam dunk, and many voters in Maine remain open to an alternative. Importantly, Maine voters (and most American voters) want “change” and while much has been written about the recent actions of President Trump, Senator Collins, Governor Mills, and Graham Platner’s interesting rise, little has been written about the voter’s desire for substantive change. That is, real policy and/or systemic change. Even if voters can’t fully articulate it, most want to do more than simply change who we elect. Most want to see changes to our political and governing systems, understanding that without them we’re unlikely to tackle our nation’s most pressing challenges. I’ve attempted to make the case for substantially reforming our governing practices and institutions but have been largely ignored by the press. As we enter our nation’s two hundred and fiftieth year, I hope that you’ll agree that a deeper discussion of our government's shortcomings and possible fixes is worthier than just stories about who has raised the most money, is ahead in the polls, or has made the most outrageous statements. A lot, including a free and journalistically ethical press, is riding on whether we make or ignore the right kind of changes in the coming three to seven years.Best,David Costello[costelloforsenate.com.](https://costelloforsenate.us22.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d37adbc910a9a40e00b14f5&id=544b376c07&e=5d7176e969)

subject: This is going to break a lot of hearts
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the NRSC
body:

name: Mark Kelly
subject: It hasn’t always been easy
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
Growing up, my parents sometimes struggled to make ends meet. In the Navy, I put my life on the line every time I took off. And at NASA, it’s no small task to launch into space.
#

Friend, I’ve got a free minute on the schedule here. That might not seem like a lot of time, but with everything happening lately, trust me: It’s a gift.
With that minute, I just wanted to write to say thank you (and make a small request).
Life hasn’t always been easy. Growing up, my parents sometimes struggled to make ends meet. In the Navy, I put my life on the line every time I took off. And at NASA, it’s no small task to launch into space.
When Gabby was shot... Well, that wasn’t easy either.
But as a kid, I always had my brother Scott. In the Navy, I had a whole squadron backing me up. At NASA, I had my crew with me and mission control support. And when Gabby was injured, it seemed like the whole country was rooting for her.
It’s been another crazy year, and an especially crazy month. But I’ve been so, so lucky these past few weeks because I have you. It’s an incredible comfort knowing that you and a ton of others have been supporting me.
Thank you. Truly.
Honestly, that support should be enough. I wish I didn’t need to ask more of you. But with the full weight of the executive branch bearing down on me, that’s what I have to do.
I have to ask you to do a bit more.
Tomorrow, our final FEC deadline of the year hits. We’ve got a steep climb to hit our goals before then — but together, we can do it. And by hitting those goals, we’ll send a message that Trump can’t ignore.
We’re not going anywhere.

name: LCV Year-End Deadline
subject: This is urgent, Peter: we’re running short, and threats to our climate are mounting in January.
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTMzNDU2NDIS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjM2MDI4NzgwMAS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
https://links.messages.lcv. We’re running out of time, Peter. Hundreds of people from around the country have stepped up today for Giving Tuesday, but we’re still running short of the 1,000 members we need to unlock an additional $100,000 for our work before midnight tonight. And with the Trump administration accelerating some of the most extreme anti-environment, pro-polluter attacks in modern history,falling short is simply not an option. We’re asking you, Peter: will you renew your LCV membership right now while membership is only $5 to help us unlock an additional $100,000 to oppose the Trump administration’s attempts to exploit our public lands and roll back climate progress? https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/X6bzs~qK~ This isn’t just about hitting a number. It’s about having the resources we need to challenge these increasingly reckless orders and attempts to shred environmental safeguards — and stop the polluter handouts that Trump and his allies are fast-tracking. RENEW YOUR MEMBERSHIP >> https://links.messages.lcv. Every single person who steps up today is critical to our efforts — here’s why this Giving Tuesday is so important: Trump is trying to erase the scientific and legal foundation of climate action. By dismantling the Endangerment Finding, which affirms that greenhouse gas emissions harm our health and welfare, Trump’s EPA would hand fossil fuel companies a free pass to spew climate pollution into our air. He’s also ending the program that required big polluters to report their pollution, making it nearly impossible to track what they’re spewing or hold them accountable.
Decades of established pollution protections are being peeled away. More than a dozen rules that keep toxic pollution out of the air we breathe and water we drink to protect our health are on the chopping block, tossed aside to allow fossil fueled power plants to cut corners and shift the burden of their damage onto our communities.
The Trump administration is giving away the Arctic to corporate polluters, working to allow more drilling in one of the planet’s last intact ecosystems. Mining roads carved through national parks and preserves. Fire-sale auctions in critical ecosystems. Hundreds of millions of acres of U.S. waters off Alaska potentially opened to drilling. It could do irreparable damage to wildlife, our climate, and Alaska Native communities. We’re working every day with our 30 state affiliates, organizing on the ground, exposing backroom deals and corruption, rallying voters, and defending the treasured and unique places that define our country. But meeting this moment requires resources — especially as we go up against big polluters and fossil fuel opponents. This $100,000 match challenge, and how many people step up this Giving Tuesday, will determine how hard we can push back. Peter, your renewal right now powers our work to protect people and the planet. Will you renew before MIDNIGHT TONIGHT to help keep this movement strong when it matters most? $5 is all it takes. https://links.messages.lcv. Every contribution brings us closer. And the clock is ticking. Thanks for standing with us, Chris Brooks
Vice President of Membership
League of Conservation Voters This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. body:
We can’t afford to lose.

# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/2365?source=&t=1&akid=233%2E124072%2E6TqcFr)
Peter — in 2026, North Carolina will hold the most competitive U.S. Senate election in the nation, and the candidates couldn’t be more different: **Roy Cooper** served our state as Governor, Attorney General, and a legislator before that. He **expanded Medicaid** to get more than 700,000 North Carolinians health insurance, stood up for abortion access, and fought for our public schools and students. **Michael Whatley** is a former Big Oil lobbyist and Washington D.C. insider who fully supports the Republican bill that **will rip Medicaid away** from millions of Americans and is putting North Carolina’s entire health care system in jeopardy. If he’s elected, he’ll be nothing more than a yes-vote for the GOP’s dangerous agenda. As North Carolina’s Governor, my top priority is serving the best interests of the people of this state. I _know_ that my friend Roy has those same interests in mind and will fight for them every day on the floor of the U.S. Senate. That’s why he has my strong support in this toss-up race. _But he needs yours, too._ **[Whatley has big-money donors and PACs pouring money into NC on his behalf. This could even become the first-ever _billion-dollar_ Senate race. Roy is counting on your grassroots support to fight back. body:
Targeting vulnerable kids gives these Republicans the attention and self-importance that all bullies crave.
#
House Republicans just passed one of the most extreme anti-LGBTQ bills that has ever come before Congress. If it becomes law, it will imprison parents and healthcare professionals.
This policy isn’t just cruel. It’s radical.
If I had come out four or five years before I did, my parents would have done the exact same thing that they did when I came out to them at 21. They would have gone and talked, first, to their pastor and, second, to a health care professional. They would have supported me — and **if this bill were law, they would have been put in jail.**
For some of my Republican colleagues, these attacks on families and doctors are the point. Targeting vulnerable kids gives these Republicans the attention and self-importance that _all bullies_ crave.
But that’s not what Congress is for. Our job should be working to improve the lives of the people who elected us — and that’s what I’ve been focused on every day.
**As long as Republicans hold control of the House, Mike Johnson and Donald Trump’s extreme agenda will continue unchecked.**

| | | | | | Peter,
In 2017, I first ran for the school board with a simple goal: put students first.
But that meant challenging the status quo and shaking up the system.
With your help and by building new coalitions across lines of difference, we have done just that and helped LAUSD become a leader in school district innovation.
In the last year, we:
* Enacted a district wide cell phone ban already seeing success in increasing student performance, behavior, mental health, and classroom engagement.
* Posted the highest academic performance in LAUSD history on state tests.
* Unanimously passed my resolution to modernize systems for family and community use of district facilities and property, benefiting families, nonprofit programs, and our community partners.
* Began modernizing outdated systems and digitizing records and forms to improve LAUSD’s operational efficiency.

When we announced re-election, we set out an ambitious goal to demonstrate our campaign’s broad support. And with less than 36 hours left before our first critical fundraising deadline I can announce we are just $8,514 from our goal!
I know you are being inundated with emails all saying the same thing, but would you consider giving even [**$5, $25, or $50 to help us reach our critical end of year goal?**](https://nickmelvoin.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e47425f168c0b7b00df186831&id=53465413a0&e=3cf484ad56)

body:
#

I’m the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in a state Trump won. And this U.S. Senate race in Georgia will be the most competitive and most expensive in the nation.
So if you’re upset by what's being done to our country right now and you're ready to fight back, please chip in what you can to support my campaign here in Georgia.
**Here’s the link to donate:**[**https://act.electjon.com/go/donate**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-dec25.lXrKfY&refcode=em251230-3-f&t=1&akid=1355%2E5691347%2ECYWC0m)
Otherwise, let me remind you why I ran for the Senate — and why this moment is even more urgent.
Before I was elected, I led investigations of corruption and human rights abuses worldwide. We exposed wrongdoing in countries where criticizing the government is dangerous, where whistleblowers and witnesses will only meet in secret, where protest carries the risk of prosecution.
More and more, the atmosphere under Trump reminded me of those places where dissent was silenced by intimidation.
Trump’s rise wasn’t just a crisis. It was a warning.
I ran for Senate because I saw the danger in electing someone so profoundly unfit for the presidency and I wanted to confront the corruption that made his rise possible. We defeated him, and I won.
But now returned to power, this President is staging a power grab unprecedented in our history:
* He’s freed violent criminals who attacked the Capitol on his behalf.
* Stacked key agencies with loyalists — and called on them to investigate his political opponents.
* Threatened to take news broadcasters off the air unless they met his demands for more favorable news coverage.
* And even called for elected Democrats to be EXECUTED.

**This is not a drill and it’s not a bad dream. As citizens, it is the test of our lifetimes.**
In 2020, the pundits said flipping a Republican Senate seat in Georgia couldn’t be done. But we built one of the strongest voter mobilization programs in Senate campaign history — and _we won._ That victory won the Senate majority.
Now we must win again. And _we will win again._
Just like last time, I can’t do it alone.
So I’m asking:
[**Please make a contribution to my reelection campaign today, of $10 or any amount that works for you.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-dec25.lXrKfY&refcode=em251230-3-f&t=2&akid=1355%2E5691347%2ECYWC0m)
The average online donation to our campaign is around $27. Many give less. Some give more.
All that matters is that lots and lots of people are contributing what they can to power our grassroots campaign. Please, contribute today.
